title: No committed golden capture: the byte-identity gate has nothing to compare against
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu — config/legacy_features_capture.php and tests/fixtures/features-production-2026-09/ are both ABSENT at 4a2a57b (verified: `ls config/ | grep -i legacy` empty; tests/fixtures holds only adhan-*, iqama-*, receipts-c0f6a72). server-plan.md §7.1 and §7.2 require both.
scenario: S2a ships. §7.2's gate says "Verified byte-identical against the capture before S2b runs" and §8.2's LegacyFeaturesContractTest says "golden fixtures are the committed PRODUCTION capture". There is no capture in the repo. The only bytes anyone has captured live in a session scratchpad at /private/tmp/claude-501/<session-uuid>/scratchpad/s2-prod-capture/fixtures/ — a per-session macOS temp directory that is wiped when the session ends. When the engineer writes LegacyFeatures a week later, the fixture is gone and the honest options are (a) skip the diff, or (b) re-capture from a production that has since had org rows edited, which freezes the WRONG bytes as the golden. Either way the Burlington iPhone on v2.5 b44 gets a drawer whose contract nobody ever diffed, and the first symptom is a support ticket about a missing tile.
why_it_matters: Byte-identity is the entire promise of S2a and it is unfalsifiable without a committed record of what production actually serves today. The capture is also perishable in a way code is not: the moment a SuperAdmin flips a switch or an admin edits the pivot screen (still live until S2b), the ability to record the pre-cutover truth is gone forever.
suggested_fix: Commit the nine raw bodies now, verbatim, before anything else in S2 lands — copy the eight features-org-*.json plus the org-17 empty body from the scratchpad into tests/fixtures/features-production-2026-09/{id}.json, and generate config/legacy_features_capture.php from them in the same commit. Record the RAW bytes, not a re-serialised parse: production emits the apostrophe as the escape sequence ’ (od -c on features-org-1.json shows `Q u r \ u 2 0 1 9 a n`), and a generator that round-trips through a decoder and back can silently change that.

verification.corrected_title: No committed golden capture, and the only capture that exists is both volatile and missing org 17
verification.notes:
Every premise verified at 4a2a57b. `ls config/` has no legacy_features_capture.php; `git ls-files | grep -iE 'legacy|cutover'` returns only the plan command, the report command, the middleware and their tests; tests/fixtures/ holds only adhan-*, iqama-*, generate-adhan-vectors.mjs and receipts-c0f6a72. server-plan.md §7.1 places BOTH the capture and config/legacy_features_capture.php in the S1 deploy — i.e. in this branch — and §7.2 makes 'verified byte-identical against the capture' the gate before S2b. The only bytes anywhere are at /private/tmp/claude-501/<session-uuid>/scratchpad/s2-prod-capture/fixtures/, a per-session macOS temp dir.

The raw-byte warning is correct and I reproduced it: `od -c` on features-org-1.json gives `Q u r \ u 2 0 1 9 a n` — production escapes the apostrophe. I'd add a second round-trip hazard the finding does not name: slashes are escaped too (`"mime_type":"image\/svg+xml"`, and every icon URL), so a generator that decodes and re-encodes with JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES also loses byte-identity.

TWO ADDITIONS that strengthen the fix, both verified by listing the capture directory:
(1) The scratchpad capture is INCOMPLETE against §7.1's own list. There is no features-org-17.json and no v1-settings-org-17.json. Org 17 is the single org whose body provably changes at the cutover (see BI-3), and it is the one org with no golden to diff against. Copying the eight files across would freeze a capture that cannot catch the only regression it needs to catch — the empty body `{"status":"success","data":[]}` has to be recorded explicitly.
(2) The capture compresses harder than the finding assumes, which makes committing it cheap: I diffed id/name/key/created_at/updated_at/icon.id/icon.original_url across all eight bodies and they are IDENTICAL in every org. The only per-org variation is `pivot.masjid_id` and `pivot.is_available` (file sizes differ by exactly 11 bytes between one-digit and two-digit org ids — 1 byte × 11 rows). So the golden is one shared catalogue block plus nine (masjid_id, is_available[11]) tuples, org 17's being the empty list.

Rating stands at must_fix: the record is perishable in a way code is not (the pivot admin screen is live until S2b, and any SuperAdmin switch flip changes the derived side), and it is the sole falsifier for the whole lens.

title: app-features:cutover-plan raises no finding in the only direction production actually differs — the migration would reverse five recorded SuperAdmin decisions at BISS and re-open a closed public contact form
location: app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:259 (`if ($pivotValue !== false) { continue; }`), :256 (side_effect is 'None: nothing is switched off.' whenever the pivot is ON), :326 (writesFor returns [$key => $pivotValue])
scenario: Every conflict class (a)-(d) is gated behind `$pivotValue === false`. All 13 differing pairs on production run the OTHER way — pivot ON, switch OFF — so the command prints ZERO blocking findings while the migration is about to write 13 ON-ward overrides across five organisations. Confirmed read-only on production: masjid 18 (Burlington Islamic Sunday School, org_type=school, parent 1) carries capability_overrides {"zakat":false,"events":false,"gallery":false,"website":false,"about_us":false,"programs":false,"prayer_times":false,"announcements":false,"contact_requests":false,"push_notifications":false} and pivot ids 6-11 ON. writesFor() therefore returns about_us=true, gallery=true, announcements=true, services=true, donation_link=true, contact_requests=true — five of them reversing an explicit, ledgered SuperAdmin decision, and contact_requests=true RE-OPENS the public contact form that was deliberately closed. The plan's "Also means" column for each of those rows reads "None: nothing is switched off." Orgs 14, 16 and 19 get donation_link=true and services=true the same way (the plan calls out only Intellicor's case, in prose, at §7.3).
why_it_matters: The command's stated purpose is that nobody discovers a module change in an app. On today's data it certifies a clean plan while the migration hands six organisations screens their admins were deliberately denied and turns a public intake form back on. A re-opened contact form starts accepting messages into an inbox nobody at BISS is watching.
suggested_fix: Add a class (e): pivot ON while the switch is OFF. Make it BLOCKING whenever the write would flip a key that is explicitly present in capability_overrides (an override is a decision on record; a type default is not), and a notice when it merely grants a type-default-off module. Print the ON-ward consequence in the same voice as SIDE_EFFECTS ("Admins regain the About Us editor", "PUBLIC INTAKE RE-OPENS: the website and app contact forms start accepting messages again"). Extend AppFeatureCutoverPlanTest with an org whose overrides say false and whose pivot says on.

verification.corrected_title: app-features:cutover-plan raises no finding in the only direction production differs: twelve ON-ward writes, four of them reversing explicit overrides at BISS, every one labelled "None: nothing is switched off"
verification.notes:
CONFIRMED, and this is the strongest finding in the set. Verified end to end against HEAD and live production.

Code: `if ($pivotValue !== false) { continue; }` at AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:259 gates conflict classes (a), (b) and (d). Class (c) is raised before the loop and only for an org with NO rows at all. `side_effect` is hardcoded to 'None: nothing is switched off.' whenever the pivot is not false (:254-257). `writesFor` returns `[$key => $pivotValue]` at :333, so a pivot-ON row proposes an ON-ward write with no finding attached.

Production (read-only SELECT, this session): the only pivot rows with is_available=0 anywhere are org 13 feature 1 and orgs 14/16/18/19 features 1-5. Class (a) and class (b) are therefore unreachable today. Class (d) is additionally gated on `$org->isMasjid()`, and 14/16/18 are schools and 19 is community, so it fires for org 13 alone. The command prints exactly TWO notices (org 13's Qur'an; org 17 has no rows), ZERO blocking, and 'No decision is outstanding.' — while proposing the twelve ON-ward writes that make up the rest of the thirteen differing pairs. Because §7.3 step 1 makes the migration's refusal depend on this command's blocking count, the gate cannot see the only direction production actually differs.

CORRECTIONS to the scenario. Org 18's capability_overrides is `{"zakat":false,"events":false,"gallery":false,"website":false,"about_us":false,"programs":false,"form_editing":true,"prayer_times":false,"announcements":false,"school_calendar":true,"contact_requests":false,"push_notifications":false}`. Intersected with the six keys the migration would write ON, the explicit-override reversals are about_us, gallery, announcements and contact_requests — FOUR, not five. `services=true` and `donation_link=true` at org 18 are grants of a module its org type is not offered by default (Masjid::MODULE_DEFAULTS school => false), not reversals of anything on record. Orgs 14, 16 and 19 have capability_overrides = NULL, so their donation_link=true / services=true are type-default grants too; the finding's framing lumps them under 'reversing recorded decisions'. The contact_requests=true consequence at org 18 is real and is the sharpest single item: SIDE_EFFECTS already spells it out as 'PUBLIC INTAKE CLOSES' in the other direction, and the plan prints the opposite of that as 'None'.

One mitigation worth stating: the 'Would write' column DOES print `about_us=true` etc., so the information is on screen. The defect is that it is not a finding, does not block, and the 'Also means' column actively misdescribes it. The suggested class (e) — blocking when the write flips a key explicitly present in capability_overrides, a notice when it merely grants a type-default-off module — is exactly the right shape, and matches the four/two split the data shows. The AppFeatureCutoverPlanTest gap is real: every test case in that file uses a pivot-OFF row.

title: The pivot fallback returns [] as a SUCCESS, so post-S2b orgs get an empty drawer with HTTP 200
location: plan §7.4 fallback step 2 (LegacyFeatures::fromPivot); today's shape at /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Http/Controllers/Mobile/MasjidMobileAppFeaturesController.php:38-72; evidence app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:229-240 (finding class (c)); HEAD 4a2a57b
scenario: S2b deletes the provisioning pivot writes (MasjidsController.php:73-79, OnboardingController.php:256-262), so from that day every newly provisioned org has ZERO pivot rows — and org 17 already has zero today (prod capture: pivot_rows=0). The never-5xx chain in §7.4 only moves past step 2 when fromPivot() THROWS. An empty result does not throw: it returns []. So the first time the derived step fails for one of those orgs (a bad override read, a capabilities-config blip, a transient), /features answers {"status":"success","data":[]} with HTTP 200, and MobileCache caches that for TTL_MEDIUM (600s). A Burlington iPhone on v2.5 build 44 and Play vc13 both draw the drawer straight from this array: the user sees a completely blank feature grid for ten minutes, the app reports no error, and the only trace is one Log::warning. This is the exact 2026-08-28 outage shape the controller's own comment says was made 'unrepeatable from the server side'.
why_it_matters: It converts a recoverable derivation failure into the worst user-visible outcome (blank drawer) on precisely the orgs the retirement creates, and it does it silently. The plan's own LegacyFeaturesNeverFailsTest only covers 'the pivot throws', so CI will never see it.
suggested_fix: Treat an empty pivot result as a MISS, not a success: `$rows = LegacyFeatures::fromPivot($masjid); if ($rows === []) { throw new RuntimeException('pivot empty'); }` so control falls through to features.lastgood and then fromCapture. Add a LegacyFeaturesNeverFailsTest case 'the pivot has no rows for this org' next to 'the pivot throws', and assert the response carries 11 rows, not [].

verification.corrected_title: The pivot fallback returns [] as a SUCCESS, so an org with no pivot rows gets a blank drawer with HTTP 200 on every request the derivation fails (not cached, but not self-healing either)
verification.notes:
CORE CONFIRMED. §7.4's chain only advances past step 2 when fromPivot() THROWS; [] does not throw. Verified that S2b deletes the two pivot-write sites (MasjidsController.php:72-80, OnboardingController.php:256-262, both on the §7.5 list), so every org provisioned after S2b has zero pivot rows, and org 17 already has zero today (db-rows-all-orgs.json: pivot_row_count 0, the only org so).

SCENARIO WRONG ON TWO POINTS. (1) The [] is NOT cached. In the §7.4 snippet the fallback sits OUTSIDE Cache::remember; when the closure throws, Laravel propagates and stores nothing. So there is no 600s window and no MobileCache entry to expire — but that is not a mitigation: it means EVERY request re-enters the failing derivation and re-answers [], so a persistent derivation failure gives a permanently blank drawer rather than a ten-minute one, with a Log::warning per request. (2) For org 17 specifically the fallback returns exactly what production serves today ([]), so 17 is not the org that breaks; the org that breaks is any org provisioned after S2b, whose correct answer is 11 rows.

Rating held at must_fix: the chain's entire purpose is the derivation-failure case, and step 2 silently defeats steps 3 and 4 (features.lastgood, fromCapture) for exactly the orgs the retirement creates. Suggested fix is right as written.

title: The cutover silently reverses four explicit SuperAdmin 'off' overrides at BISS and re-opens its public contact form, and the plan command raises no finding for any of it
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:259 (`if ($pivotValue !== false) { continue; }` — every finding class is gated on a pivot-OFF row), :254-256 (the side_effect column), :326-352 (writesFor returns [$key => $pivotValue] unconditionally for ids 1-5 and 7-11); plan §7.3 step 2; gate at plan §7.3 step 1; consequence verified at app/Http/Controllers/Mobile/ContactUsController.php:66 and app/Http/Controllers/Api/V1/ContactUsController.php:178; HEAD 4a2a57b
scenario: Org 18 (Burlington Islamic Sunday School) carries capability_overrides a SuperAdmin set by hand on 2026-09-13: about_us=false, gallery=false, announcements=false, contact_requests=false (plus events, website, prayer_times, zakat, programs, push_notifications). Its pivot has ids 6-11 ON. The literal A2 mapping writes the PIVOT value into the switch, so the S2b migration writes about_us=true, gallery=true, services=true, announcements=true, contact_requests=true and donation_link=true — four of them overwriting explicit false decisions, two of them (services, donation_link) flipping school-type defaults. The moment contact_requests flips true, moduleIsOff('contact_requests') stops refusing and the website and app contact forms at BISS start accepting messages again into an inbox nobody has watched since it was closed; the announcements editor and the Announcements broadcast channel reappear for BISS staff. Nothing warns anybody: the command emits findings only when `$pivotValue === false` (:259), so all six rows produce zero findings, blocking stays 0, the exit code is 0 and the migration's own refuse-if-unresolved gate passes. The table the owner reads prints those rows with side_effect 'None: nothing is switched off.' (:254-256) — literally true and completely misleading, because something is switched ON. Across all of production 12 of the 13 differing pairs run in this pivot-ON -> derived-OFF direction (14, 16, 19: Donate and Services; 18: six rows) and not one of them produces a finding; the only finding the whole fleet generates is a class (d) notice for org 13's Qur'an.
why_it_matters: The command exists so the owner sees every consequence before the migration runs, and it is blind to the direction that accounts for twelve of the thirteen real differences. §7.3 names this effect for exactly one org ('preserving Intellicor's pivot writes services=true and donation_link=true, which also hands Intellicor's admins those screens') — but Intellicor has capability_overrides: null, so those are type defaults; org 18 has explicit human decisions, four of them, and one of them gates public intake. This is the recorded 'audit destructive actions against their label' pattern: the label says nothing is switched off, the behaviour re-opens a closed public form.
suggested_fix: Add a fifth finding class (e): pivot ON while the derived value is OFF. Make it BLOCKING when the org has an explicit `false` in capability_overrides for that key (a human decided it) and a notice when it is only the org-type default. Change the side_effect column to be computed from the DIRECTION of the write, not from `$pivotValue === false`, with an ON-direction sentence per key ('PUBLIC INTAKE RE-OPENS: the website and app contact forms start accepting messages again' for contact_requests). Add an AppFeatureCutoverPlanTest case shaped like org 18 — six pivot-ON rows against explicit false overrides — asserting it reports blocking, since the existing fifteen cases all exercise the pivot-OFF direction.
ft: The cutover silently reverses four explicit SuperAdmin 'off' overrides at BISS and re-opens its public contact form, and the plan command raises no finding for any of it
notes: verifier-raised

title: The build on the phones is not in the repo and not on this machine — six lenses' client reasoning rests on a tree nobody can produce
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/New Masjid System — git history has no commit where CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 44. `git log -S"CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 43"` → acf56cd (2026-06-29); `-S"= 45"` → a7217de (2026-07-12); `-S"= 44"` → nothing. Nine commits sit between them. ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives holds only Wird archives — no Masjid archive at any build number.
scenario: Every statement in this review about "the Burlington iPhone on v2.5 build 44" — that it hard-codes /mobile/masjids/1/features and therefore sees org 1 only; that its splash catch never reaches appStatus = .home so a decode failure is a permanent white screen; that Feature.id is the only non-optional field — was read out of build 43 or build 45. The one fork in that two-week window that changes the answer is d8d8ee9 (2026-07-11, NAFIS Apex white-label), which replaced the hard-coded `/mobile/masjids/1/features` with `/mobile/masjids/\(AppConfig.masjidId)/features` and added a second iOS target pointed at org 5. If build 44 predates it, the fleet is Burlington-only. If it postdates it, there is a second App Store binary pointed at org 5 that no lens accounted for. Concretely: S2b ships on the strength of "org 1 and org 5 have zero pivot-vs-derived differences, so the App Store builds see none of the thirteen", and that sentence is true of a build nobody has opened.
why_it_matters: This is the joint the whole review pivots on. Six lenses independently reasoned about an unupdatable fleet from source they could not tie to the binary, and only one of them (old-builds, wrong_checked_ok #3) noticed, and then only as a citation error rather than as an unidentifiable build. The risk here is bounded and probably benign — org 5 is one of the three all-on masjids with zero differences either way — but the method is not, and it is the method that will be reused at S3a for the icon-envelope change, where the client decoder IS the gate. A review that cannot name the code running on the phones cannot certify a promise made to the phones.
suggested_fix: Before S2b, pull build 44's upload date from App Store Connect and bracket it against the commit dates above (43 = 2026-06-29, d8d8ee9 = 2026-07-11, 45 = 2026-07-12), then tag that commit `appstore/ios-b44` in the iOS repo so every future client claim is anchored. If the date lands after 2026-07-11, re-run the org-reachability question for org 5 explicitly. Adopt the tag-on-release habit for Play vc13 too — 8579eee is currently identified only by a commit message.

title: The one gate that would catch the whole payload cluster is a human running curl at 1am, and it has no committed baseline to diff against
location: server-plan.md §7.3 ("then curl `/features` for every captured org and diff byte- and order-sensitively. Any difference means `down()` first") against §8.2's seven tests; `app-features:verify-cutover` compares DB pivot values to DB derived values, never HTTP bytes.
scenario: Trace what each automated gate can see after the S2b migration applies its writes. `LegacyFeaturesContractTest` compares bytes but does not apply the migration's writes (§8.2: "reads the pivot before the marker and the switches after" — the switches as they stand, not as the migration leaves them). `CutoverMigrationTest` applies the writes and asserts "derived equals pivot", a DB-value comparison that is blind to row order, to the U+2019 in `name`, to `is_available` arriving as a boolean, and to the eleven-row count. `verify-cutover` is the same DB-level comparison. So the composite event the promise is actually about — the bytes on the wire, after the writes land — is asserted by exactly one thing: a person typing curl, comparing against a capture that is not in the repository. Concretely: the derivation emits registry order (10,9,6,1,2,3,4,5,7,8,11) instead of 1..11. Every planned test passes. verify-cutover prints zero differences, because every DB value does match. Play vc13 on Burlington reaches for Qur'an in the top-left tile and taps Announcements, and the only thing that could have caught it was an operator eyeballing a diff against a file that does not exist.
why_it_matters: This is my answer to "which single test would most reduce the risk", and it is why I would not ship yet. Six lenses produced roughly forty findings about the payload — order (BI-2, OB-4, SEQ-7), the eleven rows and the integer (BI-6), the apostrophe and the encoder flags (BI-8, R4), the unsimulated postcondition (OB-6), empty-as-success (R1, N5-02) — and a single test kills all of them at once, because they are all the same failure: the bytes after the writes are not what the bytes before the writes were. Splitting that assertion across a byte test that skips the writes and a value test that skips the bytes means no test can fail on it.
suggested_fix: Fuse them. title: The only row ORDER the branch supplies is registry order (10,9,6,1,2,3,4,5,7,8,11), not feature_id order
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/config/app_menu.php (`sections`) and app/Support/AppMenu.php:visibleItems()/sections()
scenario: The derived /features is written by walking AppMenu's registry — the one ordered structure the branch offers. config/app_menu.php orders sections main → worship → about, giving legacy ids 10, 9, 6, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11. After a registry-ordered cutover the grid becomes Announcements, Services, Donate, Qur'an, Hadith, Adhkar, Qibla, Tasbih, About Us and the two overflow rows become Gallery and Contact Us. The core is real. config/app_menu.php `sections` main→worship→about does yield legacy ids 10,9,6,1,2,3,4,5,7,8,11, and all eight captured production bodies are in feature_id order 1..11 (verified by extracting "feature_id" from each fixture). `Masjid::features()` at app/Models/Masjid.php:653 is confirmed a bare belongsToMany with only ->withPivot('is_available') and no orderBy, so today's order is incidental and the suggested `orderBy('mobile_app_features.id')` pin is a good fix.

That is precisely the ordered, id-keyed public structure the finding says the branch does not have, and it sits in the cutover file an implementer of LegacyFeatures is most likely to be reading. Two scenario corrections, both verified against the SHIPPED build (burlington-masjid-Android `master`, commit 5f1aa80 "vc13 is live"), not the unshipped r0 tree:

title: Org 17 goes from [] to 11 rows and `app-features:cutover-plan` exits 0 saying "No decision is outstanding"
location: app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php — planFor() finding class (c) is constructed with `$this->finding('c', false, ...)` (blocking=false); writesFor() returns [] when `$pivotValue === null`; emitTables() prints "No decision is outstanding" and returns SUCCESS when `$summary['blocking'] === 0`
scenario: Org 17 (ZZ QA Sandbox, masjid, capability_overrides NULL) has no pivot rows, so /features/17 serves `{"status":"success","data":[]}` today. After the marker flips, every one of the eleven ids derives ON from masjid MODULE_DEFAULTS, so the body becomes 11 full rows. `writesFor` returns [] for a null pivot, so the migration writes no override for 17 — there is no mechanism anywhere in the branch by which 17 can keep serving []. Meanwhile the command's own class-(c) finding is non-blocking, so `app-features:cutover-plan` exits 0, prints "No decision is outstanding. Notices above are for information only", and §7.3 step 1 ("Refuses to run if cutover-plan finds an unresolved conflict") lets the migration through. A TestFlight tester on 17 opens the app to an empty drawer one day and an 11-tile grid the next; no error, no log line, no decision on record.
why_it_matters: The command's docblock names this as "the ONLY change an installed build can see" and then classifies it as the one thing that cannot stop the deploy. §7.4 says the no-rows case is "owner-resolved per org; OQ-5" but nothing in the code reads a resolution for it: isResolved() is keyed by module key, and class (c) is raised with `key => null`, so `config/app_feature_cutover.php` cannot express an answer for it. The blast radius today is one QA org, but the gate is the product and it is wrong.
suggested_fix: Make class (c) blocking, and give it a resolvable key so the owner can actually answer it — e.g. `$resolutions[$orgId]['_no_rows'] = 'serve_defaults' | 'serve_empty'` — and have the migration write the 11 explicit overrides for `serve_defaults`, or record 17 as a no-derive org for `serve_empty`. At minimum, refuse to print "No decision is outstanding" while any class-(c) notice stands.

verification.notes:
Every mechanical claim verified at HEAD. finding('c', false, null, ...) at AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:234-239 — blocking=false, key=null. writesFor() returns [] on `$pivotValue === null` at :328-330. emitTables() prints 'No decision is outstanding. Notices above are for information only.' and returns SUCCESS whenever blocking===0, at :599-601. isResolved() at :485 keys on `$resolutions[orgId][$key]`, so a finding raised with key=null can never be resolved in config/app_feature_cutover.php. 'A TestFlight tester on 17 opens the app to an empty drawer one day and an 11-tile grid the next' is not a scenario that exists; MEC TestFlight is org 13, whose body is preserved. No installed app breaks here, which is why this is should_fix and not must_fix.
(2) 'no decision on record' is wrong. The class-(c) notice IS printed, and its wording is good ('the only change an installed build sees'). And `--conflicts-only` does NOT hide org 17: the skip at :549 is `findings === []`, and org 17 has a finding. The owner is told.

title: There is no conflict class for "the pivot would turn a deliberately switched-off module back ON", and the side-effect column says the opposite
location: app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php — planFor(): `if ($pivotValue !== false) { continue; }` guards every finding; the row's `'side_effect' => $pivotValue === false ? SIDE_EFFECTS[$key] : 'None: nothing is switched off.'`; emitTables(): `if ($this->option('conflicts-only') && $orgPlan['findings'] === []) continue;`
scenario: Org 18 (Burlington Islamic Sunday School, school) has capability_overrides that deliberately switch OFF announcements, about_us, gallery, contact_requests (plus website/events/programs/zakat/prayer_times/push_notifications), and its school defaults leave services and donation_link off. Its pivot has ids 6-11 ON. `writesFor` therefore writes announcements=true, about_us=true, gallery=true, contact_requests=true, services=true, donation_link=true. That is six SuperAdmin decisions reversed at one org — including `contact_requests`, whose own SIDE_EFFECTS entry says "PUBLIC INTAKE CLOSES" in the other direction: this write REOPENS a public contact form BISS closed, and restores the Announcements broadcast channel and the About Us and Gallery editors. Because every one of those rows has `$pivotValue === true`, planFor() hits `continue` before raising anything, so org 18 produces ZERO findings, `--conflicts-only` omits org 18 from the output entirely, and in the full table each of those six rows reads "Also means: None: nothing is switched off." The same mechanism hands Al-Razi (14), Intellicor (16) and MAS Youth (19) services=true and donation_link=true — twelve modules switched back on across four orgs, none flagged. §7.3 mentions this for Intellicor only, in prose, as a "known effect to restate for the owner".
why_it_matters: The /features bytes ARE preserved for org 18 — that is exactly the problem. Byte-identity is bought with six silently reversed admin decisions, and the tool whose whole purpose is to surface the cost prints "nothing is switched off" on precisely those rows. A BISS parent starts getting a contact form that was closed on purpose, and nobody chose that.
suggested_fix: Add a conflict class (e): pivot ON where the derived switch is currently OFF, i.e. the write flips a module from off to on. Raise it blocking for the keys with a public or staff-visible consequence (contact_requests, announcements, services, donation_link) and as a notice otherwise, and give it its own SIDE_EFFECTS_ON sentences ("the public contact form reopens", "admins regain the Gallery editor"). Fix the side_effect column so a row that changes a switch never reads "None: nothing is switched off", and make `--conflicts-only` key off `agrees === false` as well as findings, so org 18 cannot be the one org the conflicts view hides.

verification.corrected_title: Pivot ON over a switched-off module writes twelve silent switch reversals, captioned "nothing is switched off"
verification.notes:
Every mechanical claim verified. `if ($pivotValue !== false) { continue; }` at AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:259 guards all three finding classes. The side_effect ternary at :254-256 emits 'None: nothing is switched off.' on exactly the rows where pivot is TRUE — including the rows that flip a switch from off to on. `--conflicts-only` skips on `$orgPlan['findings'] === []` at :549.

The org-18 arithmetic is exactly right and I re-derived it from db-rows-all-orgs.json plus MODULE_DEFAULTS: overrides are {zakat, events, gallery, website, about_us, programs, prayer_times, announcements, contact_requests, push_notifications} all false, plus form_editing/school_calendar true. School defaults leave services and donation_link false. Pivot ids 6-11 are all 1. So writesFor emits donation_link=true, about_us=true, gallery=true, services=true, announcements=true, contact_requests=true — six, four of them reversing an explicit SuperAdmin override. Ids 1-5 are pivot-false but org 18 is a school, so the class-(d) branch's `$org->isMasjid()` guard is false and it `continue`s: org 18 produces ZERO findings and IS omitted entirely by --conflicts-only. Orgs 14/16/19 each get donation_link=true and services=true the same way. Twelve reversals across four orgs, none flagged. The contact_requests SIDE_EFFECTS string really does read 'PUBLIC INTAKE CLOSES' while this write reopens the form.

RATING CORRECTED to should_fix. Against the stated rubric nothing here qualifies as must_fix: byte-identity is KEPT at all four orgs (that is the point of the write), no installed app breaks, no data is lost, the endpoint does not fail. There is also a partial workaround the finding does not acknowledge — the default full table prints Pivot=on, 'Switches today'=OFF and 'Would write'=X=true on the same row, so a careful reader can see the flip; what is broken is that the 'Also means' column then contradicts those three columns, the gate never asks, and --conflicts-only hides the worst org. The suggested class (e) with SIDE_EFFECTS_ON sentences, plus keying --conflicts-only off `agrees === false`, is the right fix and I'd keep the suggestion verbatim.

title: `show_in_app` and `hide_everywhere` are synonyms: a resolution clears the block and is then never read
location: app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php — isResolved(): `return in_array($decision, ['show_in_app', 'hide_everywhere'], true);`; writesFor() writes `[$key => $pivotValue]` regardless and adds `$writes['giving'] = false` when `isResolved($org, 'giving')`; tests/Feature/AppFeatureCutoverPlanTest.php:308 `an_owners_resolution_clears_a_blocking_decision` exercises only `hide_everywhere`
scenario: An owner is handed a class-(a) blocker: "legacy id 11 is OFF in the pivot, but contact_requests still holds 40 received messages". They mean to keep the tile, so they write `17 => ['contact_requests' => 'show_in_app']`. The plan turns green. The migration writes `contact_requests => false` — the pivot value, unchanged — so the Contact Us tile stays gone AND the public intake form closes, which is precisely what `show_in_app` was chosen to prevent. Worse on id 6: `show_in_app` for `giving` satisfies the `isResolved` branch in writesFor and adds `giving => false` to the writes at an org with a connected Stripe account — the exact write MasjidsController::setCapability refuses by hand at line 314.
why_it_matters: The command demands a decision in a two-word vocabulary and then implements one of the two words as the other. Nothing in the code reads the value of the resolution, and no test covers `show_in_app`, so the bug is invisible to the suite. Today no production org is in class (a) or (b) — orgs 14/16/18/19's OFF rows are worship ids 1-5 (class d) and org 13's is id 1 — so this is latent, but it fires the first time any org gets a shared key switched off in the pivot.
suggested_fix: Read the value. `show_in_app` must make writesFor emit `[$key => true]` (and never `giving => false`); `hide_everywhere` keeps today's behaviour. Add a test for each word asserting the opposite writes, and make the plan reject any value that is not one of the two rather than treating an unknown string as unresolved.

verification.notes:
Confirmed in full. isResolved() at AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:487 is `in_array($decision, ['show_in_app','hide_everywhere'], true)` — the two words are interchangeable. writesFor() at :326-352 never reads the decision: for a non-donate key it returns `[$key => $pivotValue]` unconditionally, so `show_in_app` on a class-(a) blocker writes the pivot's FALSE and hides the tile and the public form — the opposite of what the word says. The giving branch at :347 is worse: `if ($this->givingEvidence($org) === [] || $this->isResolved($org, 'giving'))` adds `giving => false`, so `show_in_app` for giving satisfies the same branch and writes giving=false at an org with a connected Stripe account, which is the write MasjidsController::setCapability refuses by hand (the precondition is at :316, not :314 — minor location drift in the finding).

Test coverage claim verified: `grep -rn 'show_in_app|hide_everywhere' tests/ app/` returns only AppFeatureCutoverPlanTest.php:318 (hide_everywhere), the in_array at :487 and the help line at :594. `show_in_app` is never exercised.

Latency claim verified too: no production org is in class (a) or (b) today. The only pivot-false rows in the capture are worship ids 1-5 at orgs 14/16/18/19 (schools/community — the class-(d) branch's isMasjid() guard is false, then `continue`) and org 13's id 1 (class d, masjid). So no class-(a)/(b) finding can fire on today's data, and the bug is latent until the first shared key goes off in the pivot. should_fix is the right rating.

title: The derived contract needs all 11 rows including is_available:0, and the only non-filtering accessor is private to a console command
location: app/Support/AppMenu.php — visibleItems() and sections() FILTER by itemIsVisible(); the only unfiltered accessor is `legacyAvailability(Masjid, int)`, and the only loop that walks ids 1..11 through it is the private AppFeaturesCutoverPlan::planFor()
scenario: Every production fixture serves ELEVEN rows with `pivot.is_available` as 1 or 0 — org 14 sends ids 1-5 with is_available:0, it does not omit them. The obvious reuse for someone writing LegacyFeatures::rows() is AppMenu::visibleItems() or sections(), both of which drop the off rows. Org 14 would then serve 6 rows instead of 11 and org 13 ten instead of eleven. vc13 filters to `is_available == 1` at read time (MenuViewModel.kt:103) so the tiles look the same — but FeatureCache.kt:38 documents that the filter is applied on READ specifically "so a change to that rule takes" effect without waiting for handset caches to turn over, and a server that stops sending the off rows silently voids that. An iOS model that decodes a fixed catalogue, or a `[Feature]` indexed by id, sees the array shrink. And the /features body diverges from the golden by hundreds of bytes on four of nine orgs.
why_it_matters: The one correct pattern — loop the eleven ids in order, ask legacyAvailability for each, emit every row — exists only inside a private method of a console command that is explicitly out of the controller's reach. Two implementations of the same contract in two files is how they drift.
suggested_fix: Extract the ordered, unfiltered eleven into one public helper (`AppMenu::legacyRows(Masjid): array<int,bool>` keyed by legacy id in capture order) and have both AppFeaturesCutoverPlan and the derived controller call it. Assert `count($response['data']) === 11` and `assertSame(0, $row['pivot']['is_available'])` for an off row — an integer, never a boolean, matching §8.2.

title: After the cutover /features becomes config-cache sensitive, and a wrong body is then pinned for ten minutes
location: app/Models/Masjid.php:458-471 moduleIsOff() fail-open branch; app/Support/MobileCache.php TTL_MEDIUM = 600; app/Http/Controllers/Mobile/MasjidMobileAppFeaturesController.php index() Cache::remember(..., MobileCache::TTL_MEDIUM, ...)
scenario: S2b writes `quran => false` into org 13's capability_overrides (MEC's pivot has id 1 OFF). moduleIsOff('quran') resolves that correctly only while `config('capabilities.quran')` is loaded. During any later deploy window where the new PHP runs against the previous config cache — which is exactly the window MODULE_DEFAULTS and AppMenu::DEFAULT_REGISTRY exist to survive, and which bin/deploy creates on every ship because it migrates before re-caching config — `config('capabilities.quran')` is absent, so moduleIsOff takes the fail-open branch and answers from MODULE_DEFAULTS['quran']['masjid'] = true: the override is not read, and derived id 1 flips from 0 to 1. One request in that window warms MobileCache::masjidKey(13,'features') for TTL_MEDIUM = 600 seconds, so the wrong body outlives the window that produced it by up to ten minutes. MEC TestFlight testers get a Qur'an tile the masjid switched off; nothing logs.
why_it_matters: Today that byte comes from a `masjid_mobile_app_features` row — a database read no config cache can misread. The cutover swaps it for a config-dependent computation whose documented failure mode (fail open, never hide) is correct for an ADMIN SCREEN and wrong for a payload that is supposed to be byte-identical. The five worship keys are the exposed set because they are new in this branch: any older config cache does not know them. A config-cache rollback (the `.env + config:cache` class of outage) makes the window arbitrarily long.
suggested_fix: Have the derived /features read overrides directly rather than through the fail-open module gate — a key present in `capability_overrides` is an explicit recorded decision and should win even when the catalogue entry is missing — or gate the derivation on the same marker check already planned and refuse to derive (falling through to the pivot, §7.4 step 2) when `config('capabilities.quran')` is absent. Whichever you pick, add a test that installs a config WITHOUT the five worship keys and asserts org 13's body is unchanged.

verification.corrected_title: The derived rows would read module state through a gate that ignores overrides when the catalogue entry is missing
verification.notes:
The mechanism is real and I verified it exactly where the finding says: Masjid::moduleIsOff() at app/Models/Masjid.php:458-471 — when `config("capabilities.{$key}")` is absent or not kind 'module', it returns `(self::MODULE_DEFAULTS[$key][$this->orgType()] ?? true) === false` with `capability_overrides` UNREAD. MobileCache::TTL_MEDIUM = 600 confirmed. bin/deploy runs `php artisan migrate --force` at line 207 and `php artisan config:cache` at line 213, so the migrate-before-recache window is real. The five worship keys are genuinely new: production's captured `capability_keys` at app_sha 3bbe500 lists 25 keys and none of quran/hadith/adhkar/qibla/tasbih. All of that is right.

But the TRIGGER is over-broad, and the correction is the difference between 'every deploy' and 'a specific mistake'. If S2a ships before S2b as §7.2/§7.3 require, then during the S2b deploy the loaded config cache is S2a's — which already knows `quran` — so moduleIsOff takes the normal branch and reads org 13's override correctly. 'which bin/deploy creates on every ship' does not by itself produce the failure. The two paths that DO produce it: (a) S1 and S2 collapsed into one deploy, so the marker is inserted at line 207 while a pre-S1 config cache is still loaded; (b) a config-cache rollback or restore of a pre-S1 bootstrap/cache/config.php, which is the `.env + config:cache` class of outage the finding cites at the end and which is its strongest ground.

Also note the ids 7-11 writes (about_us, gallery, services, announcements, contact_requests) are immune in every case — those keys predate this branch and are in any cache.

Rating stays should_fix and the fix stays right either way: a key present in capability_overrides is a recorded decision and should win over a missing catalogue entry, or the derivation should refuse and fall through to the pivot when the catalogue is incomplete. The suggested test (install a config without the five worship keys, assert org 13's body is unchanged) is the right pin.

title: The U+2019 apostrophe survives only by accident: production emits ’ escaped, and both neighbouring encoders set JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE
location: app/Http/Controllers/Mobile/MasjidMobileAppFeaturesController.php index() `return response()->json([...])` (default flags) vs app/Support/AppMenu.php payload() `json_encode($data, JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR)` and AppFeaturesCutoverPlan::emitJson() `JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE`
scenario: `od -c` on the captured production body shows the name as the twelve bytes `Q u r \ u 2 0 1 9 a n` — /features is encoded with Laravel's DEFAULT flags, so the apostrophe is escaped. Both new encoders in this branch set JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE. An implementer building LegacyFeatures who copies the flags from AppMenu::payload() one file away, or who serialises through the cutover command's JSON path, emits the raw three-byte UTF-8 `’` instead. The parsed string is identical and every JSON decoder accepts it, so no test that uses assertJson or json_decode can see it — but a byte-diff against the golden fails on org 1, 2, 5 and 13, and any client that hashes or compares the raw body (an ETag, an offline cache-validity check) treats an unchanged menu as changed. Separately: the branch's registry vocabulary is NOT the legacy vocabulary — config/app_menu.php uses `quran`, `contact`, `about_us`, `donate`, while the catalogue rows are key `qur’an`/`contact_us`/`about_us`/`donate` and name `Qur’an`/`Contact Us`/`About Us`/`Donate`. Deriving either field from the registry key renames the tile on every Android phone (MainMenu.kt:599 renders `feature.name` as the visible label) and, on a build that routes by name, breaks the destination.
why_it_matters: This is the field the lens is most specifically about and it has zero protection in the branch: no test asserts the apostrophe, no test asserts the encoding flags, and the capture that would have caught it is not committed (BI-1). The name/key divergence is worse because it looks like a natural refactor — the registry already has a key per legacy id.
suggested_fix: Keep name/key/created_at/updated_at read from `mobile_app_features` (they survive to S3a) or from the committed capture — never from config/app_menu.php. Add an explicit test asserting the raw response content contains the literal `Qur’an` escape and the key `qur’an`, and a second asserting the derived controller does not pass any $options to response()->json(). Add a comment at AppMenu::DEFAULT_REGISTRY saying the item keys are NOT the legacy keys.

verification.corrected_title: name/key must come from the catalogue or the capture, and the default JSON flags are what preserve the U+2019
verification.notes:
The encoding half is confirmed exactly. The controller (unchanged against the merge base — `git diff 4a9d60c HEAD` on it is empty) returns `response()->json([...])` with Laravel's default flags, and `od -c` on the captured body gives `Q u r \ u 2 0 1 9 a n`, so the escape is what production emits. Both new encoders in the branch set JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE: AppMenu::payload() at AppMenu.php:518 and AppFeaturesCutoverPlan::emitJson() at :535. Copying either set of flags one file over loses byte-identity on orgs 1, 2, 5 and 13. I'd add that JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES is the same hazard — production escapes `image\/svg+xml` and every icon URL — though §8.2 masks the icon object, so that one is a golden-diff issue rather than a client one.

The NAME half I verified against the SHIPPED build and it is the sharper risk, stronger than the finding states. burlington-masjid-Android `master` (commit 5f1aa80 'vc13 is live') MainMenu.kt:159-194 does `val featureName = feature.name.lowercase().replace("-","").replace(" ","")` and then a chain of `featureName.contains("quran")|contains("qur")|contains("hadith")|...` to pick the destination, and renders `feature.name` as the tile label. The Flutter client is even more literal: menu_widget.dart:65 is `Get.toNamed(availableFeatures[index]!.name!)` — the name IS the route string — and it renders `feature.name` and force-unwraps `icon.originalUrl`. So deriving `name` from the registry key would break navigation and labels on both live builds.

ONE CORRECTION to the key list: only TWO registry keys diverge from the catalogue, not four. Catalogue keys are qur’an, hadith, adhkar, qibla, tasbih, donate, about_us, gallery, services, announcements, contact_us; registry keys are quran, hadith, adhkar, qibla, tasbih, donate, about_us, gallery, services, announcements, contact. `about_us` and `donate` match exactly. The divergences are quran→qur’an and contact→contact_us. All ELEVEN names diverge from the registry keys (case and spacing), which is the bigger exposure. The fix as written is correct; the DEFAULT_REGISTRY comment should say the item keys are not the legacy keys AND not the legacy names.

title: `features.lastgood` records the last answer that did not throw, not the last GOOD answer — a wrong derivation poisons the 30-day safety net and no flush may clear it
location: app/Support/MobileCache.php:170-181 (the flushFamily docblock's "never: `features.lastgood`" rule) + flushOwnPayloads() at :203-208, read against server-plan.md §7.4's `Cache::put(masjidKey($id,'features.lastgood'), $rows, now()->addDays(30))` inside the remember closure
scenario: S2a ships and the marker lands. LegacyFeatures::rows() is subtly wrong for org 14 — say it walks AppMenu::visibleItems() and returns 6 rows instead of 11 (BI-6), or emits registry order (BI-2). It does not throw, so §7.4's remember closure returns it AND writes it to `features.lastgood` with a 30-day TTL. MobileCache::flushFamily is forbidden by its own docblock from ever forgetting that key — "A cache flush is exactly the moment it is most needed, so nothing here may forget it" — and flushOwnPayloads names FEATURES, MENU, ORGS, SHOW one at a time and never matches a prefix, so it cannot reach `features.lastgood` even by accident. The engineer notices the bad body, runs the migration's `down()` to clear the marker, and /features goes back to the pivot and looks correct. Thirty days later a DB blip takes out both the derived path and the pivot read, step 3 of the chain serves `features.lastgood`, and Al-Razi's Android drawer comes back with six tiles in the wrong order — from a body that was written during a deploy that was rolled back a month earlier. Nothing logs it as wrong; the chain logs only that it fell back.
why_it_matters: The key is named `lastgood` and the plan treats it as the last known-good answer, but nothing validates the rows before storing them: the only condition is that the derivation did not throw, which is precisely the failure mode BI-2, BI-6 and BI-8 describe. Making it unforgettable is right for availability and wrong for correctness — it converts a transient bad deploy into a 30-day landmine with no operator lever to defuse it, because the one invalidation helper in the codebase is explicitly barred from touching it.
suggested_fix: Gate the write, and give the operator a lever. Only Cache::put the lastgood entry when the rows pass the same shape check LegacyFeaturesContractTest asserts — exactly 11 rows (or exactly the captured count for that org), ids in captured order, `is_available` an int, `name`/`key` matching the capture — and log a warning and skip the write otherwise. Store the app sha or a capture fingerprint alongside the rows and ignore a lastgood entry whose fingerprint is not the running one, so a rollback retires it automatically. Add an explicit `MobileCache::forgetLastGood(int $masjidId)` (never called by flushFamily) plus an `app-features:forget-lastgood` command, so a bad entry can be cleared without waiting 30 days. Keep the never-flush-on-family rule exactly as it is.
ft: `features.lastgood` records the last answer that did not throw, not the last GOOD answer — a wrong derivation poisons the 30-day safety net and no flush may clear it
notes: verifier-raised

title: The rollback path flushes nothing, so `down()` keeps serving the bad body for ten more minutes
location: server-plan.md §7.3 step 5 ("`down()` deletes the marker, so the pivot is the source again") read against app/Support/MobileCache.php: TTL_MEDIUM = 600 at :91, FEATURES at :25, and flushFamily at :183-187 — step 4 flushes every org on the way UP and no step flushes on the way DOWN
scenario: S2b's migration runs, inserts the marker and flushes every org (step 4). The post-migration byte diff in §7.3 comes back different for Burlington — say registry order, so the grid reads Announcements, Services, Donate, Qur'an... The instruction is "Any difference means `down()` first, investigate second", so the engineer runs `down()`. It deletes the marker, and from that instant LegacyFeatures::rows() reads the pivot again — but the WRONG body is already sitting in `mobile.masjid.1.features` with up to 600 seconds left on it, and `down()` flushes nothing. Every Burlington phone that launches in the next ten minutes gets the reordered drawer from cache, after the rollback, while the engineer is watching the diff come back clean on their own freshly-warmed request. It reads as "the rollback didn't work", which is the worst possible thing to believe with your hand on a migration.
why_it_matters: The whole reason `down()` exists in this plan is to be the instant undo for a byte-identity failure, and it is the one step in §7.3 with no flush. The branch already demonstrates it knows this class of bug twice over — MobileCache::ORGS was renamed to `orgs.v2` specifically because "bin/deploy ... does not run `cache:clear`, and this store is the database, so entries written by the pre-S1 code survive the deploy", and flushMasjidAll carries a comment about ORGS having been missing from the list leaving a parent stale for ten minutes. The rollback path needs the same treatment and does not have it.
suggested_fix: Give `down()` the same step-4 flush `up()` has: walk every org and call MobileCache::flushFamilyById after deleting the marker, in that order, so no request can re-warm a derived body between the two. State it as an explicit numbered step in §7.3 step 5 rather than leaving it implied, and cover it in CutoverMigrationTest — warm the FEATURES key with a derived body, run `down()`, and assert the next request answers from the pivot rather than from cache. Same treatment for `app-features:revert-cutover`.
ft: The rollback path flushes nothing, so `down()` keeps serving the bad body for ten more minutes
notes: verifier-raised

title: The cutover migration cannot read its own resolutions file: bin/deploy migrates before it rebuilds the config cache
location: app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:479 (isResolved) and :183; bin/deploy:207 (migrate --force) vs :209 (config:clear) / :213 (config:cache); server-plan.md §7.1, §7.3 step 1
scenario: Owner resolutions live in config/app_feature_cutover.php, a NEW file that ships with the S2b migration, and both isResolved() and the summary line read it through config(). bin/deploy runs `php artisan migrate --force` at :207 and only reaches `config:clear`/`config:cache` at :209/:213, so the migration boots on the PREVIOUS release's bootstrap/cache/config.php, in which the key does not exist. Verified read-only on production right now: array_key_exists('app_feature_cutover', config()->all()) is false, and array_key_exists('app_menu', ...) is false for the same reason (both are new files). Two outcomes, both bad. (i) §7.3 step 1 makes the migration refuse when the plan finds an unresolved conflict; every owner resolution reads as unresolved, so `sudo bin/deploy` throws under `set -euo pipefail` after composer install, chown and migrate but BEFORE config:cache, route:cache and the queue-worker restart — the release is half-deployed, running new PHP against the old route cache, and the operator's reading ("the owner never resolved these") is false. (ii) If instead the blocking check is skipped, writesFor():326 silently drops `giving => false` wherever the owner resolved it, so the override set written to production and recorded in the capability ledger is not the one the owner approved. By construction this fires on every S2b deploy on which the resolutions file exists at all — the file only exists because there were conflicts.
why_it_matters: This is the one deploy that rewrites what every installed handset's drawer is derived from, and the step that is supposed to make it reversible-by-consent is the step that silently cannot see consent. The branch already documents this exact hazard twice (Masjid.php:290-299 and AppMenu.php:60-69 both say bin/deploy migrates before rebuilding the config cache) and then builds the cutover's decision store as a third config file read at migrate time.
suggested_fix: Do not reach the resolutions through config(). Either `require base_path('config/app_feature_cutover.php')` directly in the loader (present-file check, empty array otherwise), or hold them as a committed `const` the way DEFAULT_REGISTRY and MODULE_DEFAULTS already are. Make the plan command print WHICH source it read and its checksum, so `app-features:cutover-plan` on production and the migration can be compared. Moving `config:clear` above `migrate` in bin/deploy fixes the symptom but leaves the class of bug alive for the next new config file.

verification.corrected_title: Do not reach the cutover resolutions through config() at migrate time — the hazard is real, but neither named outcome can occur on today's data and nothing at HEAD misbehaves
verification.notes:
CONFIRMED mechanically: bin/deploy:207 runs `migrate --force`, and config:clear/config:cache are not until :210/:213, so a migration does boot on the previous release's bootstrap/cache/config.php and a NEW config file is invisible to it. The branch documents exactly this twice (AppMenu.php:61-65, Masjid.php:294-298). isResolved() (AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:479) and the summary line (:183) do read config('app_feature_cutover').

CORRECTED on three counts.
(1) Location/scope: there is no migration at HEAD. The only reader of the resolutions is a command an operator runs by hand — after the deploy, when the config cache is current. `git log` at 4a2a57b, `find` over app/config/database, and grep for LegacyFeatures/fromPivot/fromCapture/app_feature_cutover all confirm the S2 pieces are unwritten. Nothing at HEAD reads a resolutions file at migrate time.
(2) The cited production verification does not show what it claims. `app_feature_cutover` and `app_menu` are absent from production's loaded config because NEITHER FILE IS DEPLOYED — both are new on this branch and production runs main @3bbe500 (config/app_menu.php appears as an addition in `git diff --stat main`). That is not evidence of stale-cache blindness; it is evidence the files do not exist there.
(3) Neither outcome can occur on today's data. I read every pivot row on production with a direct read-only SELECT: the ONLY rows with is_available=0 anywhere are org 13 feature 1, and orgs 14/16/18/19 features 1-5. No organisation has a pivot-OFF row on ids 6-11, so conflict class (a) (needs pivot OFF on about_us/gallery/services/announcements/contact_requests/donation_link) and class (b) (needs id 6 OFF) can never fire, the plan reports zero blocking findings, and config/app_feature_cutover.php would not exist. There are no resolutions to lose and no refusal to trigger, so the half-deployed `set -euo pipefail` abort and the silent `giving => false` drop both require data production does not have.

KEEP: the rule is right and cheap. When the S2b migration is written, load the resolutions with `require base_path('config/app_feature_cutover.php')` or hold them as a committed const, the way DEFAULT_REGISTRY and MODULE_DEFAULTS already are for this exact reason. should_fix against S2b, not must_fix against this branch.

title: Fallback step 2 returns an empty list successfully for an org with no pivot rows, so the chain never reaches lastgood or the capture
location: server-plan.md §7.4 fallback chain (`catch { $rows = LegacyFeatures::fromPivot($masjid); }`); org 17 has zero pivot rows; §7.5 deletes the provisioning pivot writes
scenario: `fromPivot()` for an org with no `masjid_mobile_app_features` rows returns `[]` without throwing, so the outer chain accepts it and returns HTTP 200 `{"status":"success","data":[]}`. The inner catch — and therefore `features.lastgood` and `fromCapture` — is never reached. Concrete trigger that needs no exotic fault: the lastgood `Cache::put` lives INSIDE the remember closure, CACHE_STORE=database on production, and the cache table is MariaDB on a 1-vCPU box (nproc=1, pm.max_children=12); a lock-wait timeout on that single write throws out of the closure, the outer catch fires, `fromPivot` answers `[]`, and the caller sees a clean success. Today that is org 17 (ZZ QA Sandbox, confirmed zero pivot rows). After S2b it is EVERY organisation provisioned from then on, because §7.5 removes the OnboardingController pivot writes — so a masjid that launches its app three months after the cutover has an endpoint whose documented failure mode is a blank drawer. The log line says "derived path failed", never "and the answer was empty".
why_it_matters: §7.4's whole promise is that an installed build never loses its drawer. A silent empty 200 is strictly worse than a 500 for Burlington v2.5 b44 and Play vc13: both treat 200 as authoritative and draw nothing, with no retry and no error surface anywhere — server-side logs show a warning, the app store review shows an empty app.
suggested_fix: Give every step except the final capture floor a post-condition: an empty result is a failure, not an answer. Either have `fromPivot()` throw a typed exception when the org has no pivot rows, or wrap each step as `$rows = step(); if ($rows === []) throw new EmptyLegacyFeatures();`. Log the row COUNT on every fallback so an empty answer is visible in the LOG_LEVEL=warning sweep.

The lastgood Cache::put really is inside the remember closure, so a cache-store fault does convert a healthy derivation into a fallback — that trigger is sound and is the most useful part of this finding.

CORRECTED: the named client scenario does not hold.
- Org 17 is the wrong example. `[]` IS org 17's byte-identical production payload today (verified: zero pivot rows, and /features/17 serves []). Serving [] from the fallback for org 17 preserves the contract exactly; nothing breaks, and org 17 is the ZZ QA Sandbox with no shipped app. The finding's own named org is the one org where the behaviour is correct.
- "After S2b it is EVERY organisation provisioned from then on" overstates. Between S2b and S3a the marker is present, so LegacyFeatures::rows() derives 11 rows from switches; fromPivot only runs after the derivation has ALREADY thrown. A blank drawer for a new org therefore needs a double fault, not the default path. §7.6 then deletes step 2 entirely.

title: features.lastgood is written from any non-throwing build, with a 30-day TTL and no flush — a successful-but-wrong payload becomes the permanent floor
location: server-plan.md §7.4 (`Cache::put(masjidKey($id,'features.lastgood'), $rows, now()->addDays(30))` inside the remember closure); app/Support/MobileCache.php:170-178 (flushFamily deliberately never forgets it)
scenario: `rows()` has no post-condition: the only thing that makes a payload "good" is that it did not throw. Suppose the `mobile_app_features` catalogue loses rows — not hypothetical in this system: the 2026-08-28 incident was a missing media row in this exact payload, and `tenancy:canary` has already deleted media on production (memory manara-canary-media-wipe). The derivation now returns 7 rows, throws nothing, gets cached 10 minutes AND pinned into `features.lastgood` for 30 days. The catalogue is repaired within the hour and the live path is correct again. Six days later the derivation fails for any reason; the chain serves the 7-row lastgood. Play vc13 lays tiles out BY POSITION — `take(9)` then `drop(9)` — so a 7-row body renders a short first page and an empty second page, and because `flushFamily()` is explicitly forbidden from forgetting this key, no admin action, no switch flip and no deploy clears it. It ages out 30 days after the last write.
why_it_matters: The chain's last line of defence has no notion of validity, and it is the one cache entry nothing on the system can invalidate. A single bad-but-successful build is enough to make it permanently wrong.
suggested_fix: Only write lastgood when the result passes a shape check — the row count equals the captured catalogue size for that org and every row has a non-empty name/key and a non-null icon URL — and log a warning (with the count) when it does not. Stamp the entry with the release sha and the row count so `app-features:verify-cutover` and the postcheck can assert on it. Give MobileCache an explicit `flushLastGood()` for the one caller that should be allowed to (the S2b migration, after it has verified the new derivation).

verification.corrected_title: features.lastgood has no validity gate, so a wrong-but-successful build is the floor until the next successful rebuild — not permanently
verification.notes:
The core observation (rows() has no post-condition; the only thing that makes a payload 'good' is that it did not throw) is real, and MobileCache.php:170-178 plus MobileCacheFamilyFlushTest:255-280 confirm flushFamily deliberately never forgets the key.

But the headline claim — 'permanent floor', 'no admin action, no switch flip and no deploy clears it' — is REFUTED by the very line the finding quotes. `Cache::put(lastgood, $rows, 30 days)` sits INSIDE the FEATURES remember closure, so it is rewritten on every FEATURES cache MISS, i.e. at least every TTL_MEDIUM (600 s) under any traffic at all. In the finding's own timeline the catalogue is repaired within the hour; the very next miss overwrites the 7-row entry with the correct 11. The bad floor survives roughly ten minutes, not six days and not thirty. 'Nothing on the system can clear it' is false: every successful build clears it, which is exactly why flushFamily is allowed to leave it alone. And an org with no traffic never refreshes lastgood, but also never reads it.

The Play vc13 take(9)/drop(9) consequence is therefore only reachable while the LIVE path is also wrong — at which point the live path is serving the same 7 rows anyway, so lastgood is not what breaks the drawer.

RESIDUAL, and worth doing: there is genuinely no shape check before pinning. A row-count and non-null-name/key/icon assertion before the put, plus a warning with the count when it fails, costs nothing and makes the floor mean something. Downgraded to should_fix; the flushLastGood() suggestion is reasonable but should not be reached for by anything other than the S2b migration.

title: The innermost fallback's Cache::get is not inside a try, so the last step of the never-5xx chain can 500
location: server-plan.md §7.4: `$rows = Cache::get(MobileCache::masjidKey($id,'features.lastgood')) ?? LegacyFeatures::fromCapture($masjid);` sits in the body of the inner catch, unguarded
scenario: Reaching that line means the derivation threw and the pivot read threw. After S3a that is the DESIGNED state — §7.6 drops the pivot tables and removes fallback step 2, so `fromPivot` throwing is routine, not exceptional. The cache store is the database (CACHE_STORE=database, MariaDB, 1 vCPU); a lock-wait timeout or a corrupt `cache` row during the 02:40 backup makes `Cache::get` throw a QueryException. Nothing catches it: it escapes the handler and Laravel renders a 500. A Burlington iPhone on v2.5 build 44 launches, gets a 500 from the one endpoint §7.4 promises cannot 5xx, and shows whatever its error path shows — which, on a build nobody can update, is the failure this whole section exists to prevent.
why_it_matters: Four fallback steps that all return 200 is the stated contract; the code sketch has three guarded steps and one unguarded one, and the unguarded one is the one that runs when everything else has already failed.
suggested_fix: Wrap the lastgood read and the capture read in their own try, in that order, and make `fromCapture()` structurally incapable of throwing (see N5-05): pure array construction over a code constant, no DB, no cache, no config. Add the case to LegacyFeaturesNeverFailsTest — bind a cache store that throws on get as well as the derivation and pivot, and assert 200.

verification.notes:
Verified against the §7.4 sketch as written. `$rows = Cache::get(MobileCache::masjidKey($id,'features.lastgood')) ?? LegacyFeatures::fromCapture($masjid);` is in the BODY of the inner catch, and PHP does not route an exception thrown inside a catch block back into the enclosing try. So the fourth step of a chain whose whole promise is 'all four paths return HTTP 200' is the one step that can 500. The `Log::warning(...)` on the line above is exposed identically. CACHE_STORE is database on production (config/cache.php default, confirmed), so a lock-wait timeout or a corrupt cache row on that one table is a real way to throw from Cache::get while findOrFail and the derivation's own reads succeeded — the plan's 'a DB outage is out of scope' escape does not cover it, because findOrFail already succeeded.

One detail in the scenario is wrong and does not change the verdict: §7.6 says S3a REMOVES fallback step 2 ('LegacyFeatures loses fallback step 2'), so it is deleted, not left routinely throwing. The unguarded line is still the last-resort line.

The fix and the named test (bind a cache store that throws on get as well as the derivation and pivot, assert 200) are both right. Keep should_fix: it is a real defect with an obvious workaround, in a sketch not yet written into code.

title: assertWroteNothing() cannot tell a concurrent admin from itself, so a live production run can accuse the read-only command of writing
location: app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:153-154 (the before counts), :512-533 (assertWroteNothing); the command is documented as a production command in its own class docblock (:40-45) and in server-plan.md §8.3 step 9 and §8.4
scenario: An operator runs `php artisan app-features:cutover-plan` on production as §8.3 step 9 instructs. The run walks every organisation (Masjid::query()->orderBy('id')->get()) doing per-org pivot, content and giving reads; on the 1-vCPU box this takes tens of seconds — my own single read-only tinker against the same box was still running after twelve minutes under normal load, with another session's tinker alongside it. During that window a SuperAdmin flips one module switch in the admin SPA, which writes one masjid_capability_changes row through MasjidsController::setCapability. assertWroteNothing() then sees the ledger at N+1 and throws RuntimeException: "app-features:cutover-plan is read-only, but the capability ledger went from N to N+1 rows during this run." The operator sees an unhandled exception and stack trace claiming the command they were told is safe on production has just written to production — and loses the whole plan, because the throw happens after planFor() has run for every org but before emitTables()/emitJson(). The same fires if any session runs the plan twice concurrently, or if the cutover migration is ever run while a plan is open. Nothing was actually written; the message says otherwise.
why_it_matters: The class docblock stakes the command's entire credibility on this check — "this command changed nothing is checkable rather than merely intended" and "the whole reason this runs on production is that it cannot change production". A check that fires on somebody else's write turns the safety instrument into a false incident, on the one command the owner's decision is supposed to rest on. The correct operator response to that message is to treat it as a data-integrity incident, which is exactly the wrong response.
suggested_fix: Make the check name what changed rather than count it. Record MAX(id) of masjid_capability_changes and of masjid_mobile_app_features before the run; on a difference, SELECT the new rows and print them (masjid, capability, actor, created_at) with a message that distinguishes "these were written while the plan ran, by <actor>" from "the plan wrote these". Only fail hard when a new row has a null actor inside the run window on an organisation the plan touched — the signature the cutover migration itself will use. Extend AppFeatureCutoverPlanTest with a case that inserts an unrelated ledger row mid-run and asserts the command still emits its plan.

title: show_in_app and hide_everywhere write the identical thing; the owner's decision is thrown away
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:477-488 (isResolved) and :326-352 (writesFor) @ 4a2a57b
scenario:
isResolved() returns a bare bool -- `in_array($decision, ['show_in_app','hide_everywhere'], true)` -- so it answers "did the owner type something", never "what did the owner decide". writesFor() never reads the decision value at all. Two consequences, both on the writes the migration is meant to copy:

(1) For every non-6 id, writesFor returns `[$key => $pivotValue]` unconditionally (:332-334). Owner records `13 => ['announcements' => 'show_in_app']` meaning "keep the app row, keep the module". Plan goes from blocking to non-blocking (pinned by an_owners_resolution_clears_a_blocking_decision, which only ever tests 'hide_everywhere'), and the cutover writes `announcements = false` -- the exact opposite. MEC TestFlight and the Burlington App Store build on v2.5 build 44 lose the Announcements row from the drawer on their next /features refresh, and the org's admins lose the announcements editor and the Announcements broadcast channel, after the owner explicitly asked to keep them.

(2) Sharper, for id 6: writesFor :347 is `if ($this->givingEvidence($org) === [] || $this->isResolved($org, 'giving'))` then `$writes['giving'] = false`. givingEvidence is non-empty precisely when Giving has a connected Stripe account, active funds, live monthly gifts or open checkout pages. So recording `['giving' => 'show_in_app']` unblocks the plan AND writes `giving = false` at an org Stripe is still billing. MasjidsController::setCapability:314-346 refuses that flip with a 422 and a sentence naming the gift count; the cutover path has no such guard. The org's admins open Recurring Donations and the screen is gone, monthly gifts keep charging donors in Stripe, and nobody can see them to issue a receipt -- the exact harm the class docblock says must never happen.
why_it_matters: config/app_feature_cutover.php is the entire mechanism by which the owner's days-long decision reaches the code. Today it can only express 'hide_everywhere'; typing 'show_in_app' silently gets you 'hide_everywhere' plus a cleared gate. The plan's own 'Would write' column is what the owner approves, and it is wrong for the resolution the owner is most likely to pick.
suggested_fix: Make isResolved() return the decision (?string), not a bool, and split the two call sites. In writesFor(): 'show_in_app' must write `[$key => true]` (and for id 6 `donation_link => true`, giving untouched); 'hide_everywhere' keeps today's behaviour. Keep the GivingSwitch precondition unconditional -- no resolution value should be able to write `giving = false` while givingEvidence() is non-empty; that case needs the gifts cancelled first, same as the SuperAdmin screen. Add tests that assert the WRITE differs between the two values, not only that blocking drops to 0.

What survives is the weaker case: an org with a connected Stripe account or active funds but zero live gifts (givingEvidence is broader than the GivingSwitch precondition) loses the Giving screen after the owner asked to keep it.

title: config/app_feature_cutover.php cannot be read by the migration it is committed with (deploy caches config AFTER migrating)
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:479 `config('app_feature_cutover')`; /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/bin/deploy:207 (migrate --force) vs :213 (config:cache) @ 4a2a57b
scenario:
Verified on production 2026-09-15: bootstrap/cache/config.php exists (88 KB, mtime Sep 15 16:11). When Laravel's config is cached it `require`s that one file and never scans config/, so a config file that did not exist when the cache was built is absent from config() entirely -- config('app_feature_cutover') returns null, not a partial array.

Plan section 7.3 says the resolutions file is 'committed with the migration'. bin/deploy runs `php artisan migrate --force` at line 207 and `config:cache` at line 213. So on the S2b deploy the cutover migration executes against the PREVIOUS config cache, which predates the new file. isResolved() returns false for every resolution the owner recorded. Step 1 of the migration ('refuses to run if the plan finds an unresolved conflict') then throws, and the deploy aborts -- but only after the S2b code is already on the box, including the deleted Mobile App Features admin routes and the deleted SPA views (section 7.5). The operator is left with: /features still correct (marker absent, pivot still the source, so no app client breaks), an aborted deploy, and no admin screen left to edit the pivot on.

The mirror image is just as bad and hits first: the owner adds config/app_feature_cutover.php, does NOT deploy, and runs `php artisan app-features:cutover-plan` on production to check their work. Same cached config, same null, same 'N decisions still need the owner'. The owner concludes the file format is wrong and re-resolves.
why_it_matters: The gate between 'owner has decided' and 'migration may write' runs through a config() lookup that is structurally unreadable at the moment it is asked. Nothing in the branch tests this, because the test suite runs without a config cache.
suggested_fix: Do not read the resolutions through config(). Load them from a known path with a file_exists guard -- `$file = base_path('config/app_feature_cutover.php'); $resolutions = is_file($file) ? require $file : [];` -- so the answer is the same cached or not. Alternatively move resolutions into a DB table written before the deploy. Either way, add a guard at the top of the command and the migration that fails loudly when the file exists on disk but config() does not see it.

verification.corrected_title: config('app_feature_cutover') is unreadable on a config-cached box, so resolutions typed on production are ignored
verification.notes:
MECHANISM CONFIRMED, INDEPENDENTLY AND STRONGLY. bin/deploy has `set -euo pipefail` (:45); migrate --force is :207 and config:clear/:210, config:cache/:213 both run AFTER it. I verified on production read-only: bootstrap/cache/config.php exists, 88210 bytes, mtime Sep 15 16:11, and config/app_feature_cutover.php is absent there. A cached config is a single require'd file, so a config/ file added since the cache was built is simply not in config().

CORROBORATED BY THE AUTHOR'S OWN CODE. Masjid::MODULE_KEYS (:292-299) and AppMenu::DEFAULT_REGISTRY (:61-68) both carry comments describing exactly this window -- "bin/deploy merges, installs and migrates BEFORE it rebuilds the config cache, so for a stretch of every deploy the new PHP reads the previous cache" -- and both defend against it with an in-code mirror.
