title: The S2b migration reads config/app_feature_cutover.php, but bin/deploy runs `migrate --force` before `config:cache` — so a config file new in that deploy reads as null
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/bin/deploy:206-214 ("Migrations" runs before "Caches"); /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:183-185 and :479 (`config('app_feature_cutover')`); server-plan.md §7.1 and §7.3 item 1. HEAD 4a2a57b.
scenario: Production has a compiled config cache (`bootstrap/cache/config.php`, 88 KB, verified read-only on 159.65.239.51) and `CACHE_STORE=database`. Laravel 12's `LoadConfiguration::bootstrap` (read on the prod box) does `if (file_exists($cached = $app->getCachedConfigPath())) { $items = require $cached; $loadedFromCache = true; }` and then `if (! $loadedFromCache) { $this->loadConfigurationFiles(...) }` — config/*.php are never read when the cache file exists. bin/deploy's order is `git merge` → composer → chown → `php artisan migrate --force` → `config:clear` → `config:cache`. So the S2b data migration boots against the PREVIOUS deploy's compiled config, and `config/app_feature_cutover.php` — a file that lands in that same deploy — is invisible. Two outcomes, both bad. (a) The migration honours §7.3 item 1 and refuses because every conflict reads as unresolved: `set -euo pipefail` with no trap aborts bin/deploy after `git merge`, `composer install` and `chown` but BEFORE `config:clear`, `route:cache` and the queue restart. The box now runs S2b code against the S2a route cache, which still routes `/admin/masjids/{id}/features` (routes/admin.php:305-309) to `AdminDashboard/MasjidMobileAppFeaturesController`, a class S2b deletes — a SuperAdmin opening Mobile App Features gets a 500, and the queue worker is still running S2a code. (b) The migration treats "no resolutions" as "nothing to resolve" and writes the literal A2 mapping unguarded: org 18 (BISS) has six owner-resolvable rows, so Play vc13 at BISS relaunches and its `take(9)/drop(9)` tile grid loses Donate, About Us, Gallery, Services, Announcements and Contact Us at once, with every remaining tile shifted. The same root cause also hits the human step: an owner who commits resolutions and asks for `app-features:cutover-plan` to be re-run on production right after any deploy is told their resolutions did not take (AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:183-185 prints "does not exist yet").
why_it_matters: This is the one deploy in the lane that writes data derived from a brand-new config file, and the deploy script's own step order guarantees that file is unreadable at the moment it is read. The branch already knows this hazard — `AppMenu::DEFAULT_REGISTRY` and `Masjid::MODULE_DEFAULTS` exist verbatim for it, and `MobileCache::ORGS` was renamed to `orgs.v2` over the same deploy-window reasoning — but the protection was applied to the HTTP paths and not to the migration, which is the one caller that cannot fail open.
suggested_fix: Do not put the cutover resolutions in `config/`. Put them in a PHP class constant the way `AppMenu::DEFAULT_REGISTRY` and `Masjid::MODULE_DEFAULTS` are, so the autoloader (which bin/deploy refreshes with `composer install -o` before migrate, and then verifies) is the only thing that has to be fresh. Failing that, make the migration hard-refuse when `app()->configurationIsCached()` is true and `config('app_feature_cutover')` is null, with a message naming `config:cache` — and move the data write out of `migrate --force` into a separate artisan command run after the Caches step, so a refusal cannot leave the box half-deployed.

verification.corrected_title: Putting the cutover resolutions in config/ makes them unreadable to the migration that reads them — and the S2b deploy cannot then self-heal
verification.notes:
Mechanism CONFIRMED at HEAD, and stronger than the finding says in one place and weaker in another.

Confirmed: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/bin/deploy:45 is `set -euo pipefail` with no trap (grep for `trap` returns only prose in the header comment). Step order is `say "Migrations"` + `as_web php artisan migrate --force` at :206-207, then `say "Caches"` + config:clear/route:clear/view:clear/config:cache/route:cache at :209-214. Nothing between the git merge and :207 touches bootstrap/cache. Production does hold a compiled config: read-only ls of 159.65.239.51:/var/www/.../bootstrap/cache shows config.php 88210 bytes, routes-v7.php 890703 bytes (both mtime Sep 15 16:11), and .env carries APP_ENV=production, CACHE_STORE=database, LOG_LEVEL=warning. AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php reads `config('app_feature_cutover')` at :183 and :479, and `isResolved()` at :477-488 returns false for a non-array — so a stale cache is indistinguishable from "nobody has resolved anything". routes/admin.php:305-310 is the features block pointing at AdminDashboard\MasjidMobileAppFeaturesController, which §7.5 deletes, so an aborted deploy does leave the old route cache pointing at a class no longer on disk.

STRONGER than stated: the failure does not just abort once. Re-running bin/deploy re-runs migrate --force against the SAME stale config cache (config:cache never got to run), so the migration refuses again and aborts again, forever. The deploy cannot complete without a human running `php artisan config:cache` by hand — which is the one step nobody thinks to run when the message says "unresolved conflict".

REFUTED: scenario (b). The plan's §7.3 item 1 is explicit that the migration "Refuses to run (throws before any write) if app-features:cutover-plan finds an unresolved conflict", and AppFeaturesCutoverPlan's own contract is fail-closed. Nothing at HEAD supports a migration that treats "no resolutions" as "nothing to resolve", so the BISS/org-18 six-tile loss is not reachable from this cause. Drop it; it inflates the rating and is the part an author will push back on.

RATING corrected to should_fix. Neither `config/app_feature_cutover.php` nor the S2b migration exists at HEAD (`ls config/` shows app_menu.php only), so this is a design decision still open, not shipped code. The worst realistic outcome is a stuck deploy plus a 500 on an admin route that is being deleted in that same deploy — no installed app breaks and no data is lost. The fix (class constant, the way AppMenu::DEFAULT_REGISTRY and Masjid::MODULE_DEFAULTS already are) is correct and costs nothing if taken before S2b is written.

title: The production capture the whole byte-identity promise rests on is not committed — the only copy lives in a session scratchpad under /private/tmp
location: Absent from the worktree: no `tests/fixtures/features-production-2026-09/`, no `config/legacy_features_capture.php` (worktree has only `tests/fixtures/{adhan-prayer-times.json, iqama-resolution.json, generate-adhan-vectors.mjs, receipts-c0f6a72}`). server-plan.md §7.1 says both ship in the S1 deploy; §7.4 says "row order per org copied from the capture — not id order"; §8.2's `LegacyFeaturesContractTest` names them as the golden fixtures. The only copy is /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-moneebsayed-Library-Mobile-Documents-com-apple-CloudDocs-Developer/3f504d96-ebb5-41a2-afbc-3c88b332f113/scratchpad/s2-prod-capture/fixtures/. HEAD 4a2a57b.
scenario: The machine reboots, or the session ends and /private/tmp/claude-501 is cleared. At S2a there is nothing to diff `LegacyFeatures::rows()` against, so the "verified byte-identical against the capture before S2b runs" gate in §7.2 cannot be executed, and `LegacyFeaturesContractTest` has to be written against whatever production serves on the day — which, if S2a slipped, may already be derived. The specific byte that dies quietly is the U+2019 in feature id 1: production serves `name` = "Qur’an" AND `key` = "qur’an", both with U+2019, and Play vc13 routes rows BY NAME. A derivation that reconstructs the name from `config/app_menu.php`'s ASCII item key `quran`, or from a label table someone typed with an ASCII apostrophe, produces "Qur'an" — vc13 stops matching it, that tile falls through to whatever the unknown-name branch does, and every tile after it in the `take(9)/drop(9)` layout shifts one position. Orgs 1, 2 and 5 all serve id 1 ON, so it is the first tile in the grid on three organisations including Burlington.
why_it_matters: §7.4's contract is "the same bytes", and the artefact that defines those bytes is the capture. Shipping S1 without it means the S2a verification gate has no referent, and the one test named as the guard for the U+2019 cannot be written. A capture that has already been taken and validated (the pivot-vs-derived analysis, the theme_settings four-state finding, the corrected parent_id column) is sitting in a temp directory that nothing preserves.
suggested_fix: Commit the eight `/features` bodies and the eight `/v1/settings` bodies from that scratchpad into `tests/fixtures/features-production-2026-09/` in THIS S1 branch, exactly as §7.1 specifies, together with the generated `config/legacy_features_capture.php` recording per-org row ORDER and per-row id/name/key/created_at/updated_at/is_available. Note that §7.1 puts the capture in `config/` — see SEQ-1: if the derived `/features` reads it through `config()`, it inherits the same stale-config-cache window on the S2a deploy, so make it a class constant too.

verification.corrected_title: The production capture that defines the byte-identity contract is not committed — commit it in S1 while the pivot is still the source
verification.notes:
Absence CONFIRMED at HEAD: `ls tests/fixtures/` returns only adhan-prayer-times.json, generate-adhan-vectors.mjs, iqama-resolution.json and receipts-c0f6a72 — no features-production-2026-09/. `ls config/` shows app_menu.php as the only new config file — no legacy_features_capture.php, no app_feature_cutover.php. server-plan.md §7.1 does say both ship in the S1 deploy, and §8.2 names them as LegacyFeaturesContractTest's golden fixtures. The only copy is the /private/tmp scratchpad.

The U+2019 hazard is REAL and I verified the bytes myself rather than taking them on trust: fixtures/features-org-1.json row 0 is `"name": "Qur’an", "key": "qur’an"` with U+2019 in both, `"pivot": {..., "is_available": 1}` as a JSON integer, and rows in id order 1..11.

RATING corrected to should_fix, for one reason the finding misses: the capture is re-takeable. S2a is marker-gated (§7.2: "Production behaviour is unchanged because the marker row does not exist yet, so /features still reads the pivot"), so production keeps serving the pivot right up to the moment the S2b migration inserts the marker. Losing /private/tmp costs a re-capture, not the contract — so this is not data loss and not must_fix. The scenario's "if S2a slipped, may already be derived" is wrong for the same reason.

Two additions worth carrying into the fix. (a) The scratchpad holds eight /features bodies, not nine — org 17 is absent because it serves []. §7.4 makes a specific promise about orgs with no pivot rows ("the 11 rows in Burlington's captured order"), and there is no captured referent for 17 to test that against; capture it explicitly, even as an empty body. (b) The finding's own note is the important half: §7.1 puts the capture in config/, which walks straight into SEQ-1's stale-config-cache window on the S2a deploy — and `LegacyFeatures::fromCapture` is the LAST-RESORT answer in the never-5xx chain, so a null read there means `/features` answers [] and empties a vc13 drawer. Make it a class constant.

title: The S1 deploy notes have no SPA step, and the SPA carries the fix that the S2b migration will otherwise break for MEC's admins
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/DECISIONS.md:1410-1420 (three deploy bullets: "S1 is additive", the kill row, the cron — none about assets); /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/resources/vue-app/core/helpers/access.ts:6-24 (`adminScreensOff`); /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/resources/vue-app/views/dashboard/TeamView.vue:182-188; server-side source is /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Http/Controllers/AdminDashboard/TeamController.php:358-364 and app/Models/Masjid.php:523-529. HEAD 4a2a57b.
scenario: bin/deploy ships no frontend (it runs composer, migrate and the artisan caches; the SPA is a separate manual `git archive` build + rsync). The filter that keeps app-only modules out of staff sentences exists ONLY in the SPA: `TeamController::screensOff` maps `$masjid->modules_off` with no `surface` filter, and `modules_off` is `moduleOfferedByDefault($key) && moduleIsOff($key)`. For a masjid, `moduleOfferedByDefault('quran')` is true. At S2b the migration writes `quran = false` for org 13 (MEC) to preserve the pivot's Qur'an-OFF. From that instant, MEC's Team & Access screen and the SuperAdmin's user screens tell an administrator "Switched off here: Qur'an" about a screen they never had — unless the S1 SPA bundle is already on production. Nothing in the deploy notes says it has to be, and nothing ties the SPA rsync (S1) to the migration (S2b, weeks later). Separately in the same window: `app_version_settings.navigation` is the documented per-org, per-platform shell rollback "without a release", and its only control surface is the select in `AppConfigView.vue` — there is no artisan command for it (verified: `grep -rn navigation app/Console/Commands/` returns only comments in AppMenuKill). With a stale SPA the one non-release rollback lever for R1 has no UI at the moment R1 ships.
why_it_matters: The branch got the ordering dependency right in the code and the comment (access.ts spells out exactly this failure) and then left it out of the only place an operator reads before deploying. Memory `manara-spa-deploy-trap` and `manara-prod-main-divergence-and-assets` both record that bin/deploy ships no frontend; this deploy has seven changed SPA files and one of them is a correctness fix for a later stage.
suggested_fix: Add a numbered SPA step to the S1 deploy notes with the same prove-it shape as the kill step (build from a `git archive` export, rsync without `--delete`, chown, then assert the built bundle hash changed), and add a hard precondition to the S2b runbook: the S1 SPA must be live on production before the cutover migration runs. Separately, give `navigation` an artisan lever — `app-config:navigation --org= --platform= --value=` — so the shell rollback has a command the way the menu kill does, instead of depending on the SPA it is meant to be independent of.

verification.notes:
Verified end to end at HEAD, with line drift.

The server does not filter: AdminDashboard/TeamController::screensOff() at :359-364 maps `$masjid->modules_off` with no surface filter; Masjid::getModulesOffAttribute() at :523-529 is `moduleOfferedByDefault($key) && moduleIsOff($key)` over MODULE_KEYS, and MODULE_KEYS at :300-328 now includes quran/hadith/adhkar/qibla/tasbih with the comment "The app-only worship modules (`surface` => 'app'): no admin screen, no sidebar item". MODULE_DEFAULTS:370 gives `'quran' => ['masjid' => true, ...]`, so for a masjid `moduleOfferedByDefault('quran')` is true and quran lands in modules_off the moment it is switched off. The filter is SPA-only: resources/vue-app/core/helpers/access.ts exports adminScreensOff() at :18 filtering APP_SURFACE_MODULES (Capability.ts:73-79 = the five worship keys), consumed at TeamView.vue:184-186. The docblock above adminScreensOff states the failure verbatim: "after the app-features cutover writes `quran=false` for the organisations whose app menu never listed it, that is exactly what both screens would say."

The deploy notes gap is real: DECISIONS.md:1404-1419 has exactly three bullets — S1 is additive / the kill row / the cron — and no SPA step. Production fact 13 = all but id 1 means the S2b migration writes quran=false for MEC, so this fires on a real org.

The navigation half is also correct: `grep -rn navigation app/Console/Commands/ routes/console.php` returns only two comment lines in AppMenuKill.php (:20, :23). There is no artisan lever for `app_version_settings.navigation`; its only control surface is the SPA select, and UpdateAppConfigRequest.php:33 is the only validation of it.

Line drift to fix in the write-up: the DECISIONS deploy notes are :1404-1419 not :1410-1420; access.ts's adminScreensOff is :6-22 (signature at :18); TeamView.vue is :184-186; TeamController::screensOff is :358-365; Masjid::getModulesOffAttribute is :523-529 (matches). Rating should_fix is right — the harm is an administrator being told a screen they never had was taken away, which is confusing, not breaking.

title: Rolling back S2b deletes the marker but nothing flushes MobileCache::FEATURES — the cache store is the database, so phones keep the derived body for ten minutes after the rollback "succeeded"
location: server-plan.md §7.3 item 5 ("`down()` deletes the marker, so the pivot is the source again" — no flush); /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Support/MobileCache.php:95 (`TTL_MEDIUM = 600`) and :168-184 (`flushFamily`); /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/bin/deploy:209-214 (no `cache:clear`); production `.env` has `CACHE_STORE=database` (verified read-only). HEAD 4a2a57b.
scenario: S2b is live. The post-migration byte-diff finds a wrong row for org 16 (IntelliCor), so the operator runs `php artisan migrate:rollback` per §7.3. `down()` deletes the marker, `LegacyFeatures::rows()` reverts to the pivot, `app-features:verify-cutover` (which compares DB pivot against DB-derived, not the endpoint) prints zero differences, and `/api/v1/settings` — which is not cached at all; `Api/V1/SettingController::index` queries the relation directly at :81 — reverts instantly and reports the pivot's `activated_features`. Every signal the operator looks at says "rolled back". But `/features` is wrapped in `Cache::remember(MobileCache::masjidKey($id, FEATURES), TTL_MEDIUM)` on the DATABASE store, which no deploy clears and which `down()` does not touch. Play vc13 at IntelliCor cold-launches in that ten-minute window, gets the derived body again, and is still missing Donate and Services while the channel already says the rollback landed. It self-heals on the TTL, so the operator never learns the rollback was not atomic — and if the same fault recurs, they will trust the same non-proof again.

title: The kill-row deploy step's proof cannot distinguish "kill row set" from "route not deployed", and the script it cites does not exist
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/DECISIONS.md:1414-1418. `grep -rn 's1-prod-postcheck|s1-staging-check|s2-prod-postcheck|switches2-prod-check'` over the worktree returns exactly one hit — the DECISIONS line that names it. `scripts/` holds only `ship.sh`, `provision-cutout.sh` and `cutout/`. HEAD 4a2a57b.
scenario: The documented step is `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' .../api/mobile/masjids/13/menu   # expect 404`, and the commit message argues correctly that the command's exit status is not the evidence — the endpoint is. But `-o /dev/null` throws the body away, and Laravel answers 404 for an unrouted path too, with `{"message":"The route ... could not be found."}` rather than the controller's `{"status":"failed",...,"data":{}}`. So if `route:cache` did not pick up the new route — for instance because bin/deploy aborted before the Caches step, which is exactly the SEQ-1 failure — the check passes for the wrong reason. The team records that the kill lever was proven when in fact `/menu` has never been routed and the lever has never been exercised at all. At S2b they run `app-menu:restore` and discover the endpoint is 404 for a reason no command can fix. And `s1-prod-postcheck.sh`, cited in the same paragraph as the thing that "asserts the 404 for the same reason", is not in the repository.
why_it_matters: The commit that created this step did so specifically because a prose bullet is not a check. The check it replaced the bullet with is a status code that two completely different states share, and the script it defers to for rigour does not exist — so the strongest gate in the S1 runbook proves less than it reads.
suggested_fix: Make the step assert the body, not the code: `curl -s .../masjids/13/menu | grep -q '"status":"failed"'` plus a check for the `data` object — that shape only comes from `AppMenuController::unavailable()`, so it proves the route is live AND the kill is biting. Better still, order it: curl for 200 BEFORE running `app-menu:kill` (proving the route deployed), then kill, then curl for the failed envelope. Either write `s1-prod-postcheck.sh` in this branch or drop the sentence that says it asserts this.

verification.notes:
Confirmed exactly as written.

DECISIONS.md:1406-1418 is the numbered kill step; the check is `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://masjid.hopetechapps.com/api/mobile/masjids/13/menu   # expect 404`, and the paragraph does claim "`s1-prod-postcheck.sh` asserts the 404 for the same reason" at :1418. `grep -rn 's1-prod-postcheck|s1-staging-check|s2-prod-postcheck|switches2-prod-check'` across the worktree (excluding vendor/node_modules/.git) returns exactly one hit: DECISIONS.md:1418 itself. `ls scripts/` = cutout, provision-cutout.sh, ship.sh.

The two-states-one-code claim holds: AppMenuController::unavailable() at :170-178 returns `{"status":"failed","message":…,"data":{}}` with 404, which is a different body from Laravel's unrouted `{"message":"The route … could not be found."}`, and -o /dev/null discards the only thing that tells them apart. title: No test fails when /features changes shape, at any point in the S1→S2b sequence — the contract test that would ships with the change it is meant to catch
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/tests/Feature/InstalledBuildsContractTest.php:29-31 — "Scope is S1's four surfaces. `GET /features`, the biggest one, is asserted against the production capture in `LegacyFeaturesContractTest` at S2, when there is a derivation that could break it. Today it is untouched code." `LegacyFeaturesContractTest` does not exist in the worktree. routes/api.php now wraps the features route in `CountLegacyFeaturesHit`. HEAD 4a2a57b.
scenario: `/features` is the one endpoint all three named clients call on launch, and it is the only S1 surface with no contract test. The branch's own reasoning for `InstalledBuildsContractTest` — "a regression here is not a failing feature; it is a phone in somebody's pocket that stops working" — applies most strongly to the endpoint it excludes. Concretely: the S1 deploy already changes that route (it gains terminable middleware), and between now and S2a any commit touching `MobileMedia::envelope`, the `ICON_FALLBACKS` map in `Mobile/MasjidMobileAppFeaturesController.php:22-35`, or the ordering of the `features` relation goes out with nothing red. The `is_available` cast is the sharpest case: today it comes straight off the pivot as whatever the driver returns, and §7.4 requires `(int)` because Android's `FeaturesResponse` declares it an Int. A derivation that returns PHP booleans serialises `true`/`false`, Gson throws on the Int field, and vc13 gets no feature list at all — an empty drawer, which is the 2026-08-28 incident again. The test that would catch it is scheduled to be written at S2, in the same change as the derivation.
why_it_matters: A transition test written alongside the transition tests the author's understanding of the change, not the change. The whole sequence's promise is "the same bytes", and the assertion of those bytes is the one artefact deferred to the deploy that breaks them.
suggested_fix: Write the `/features` half of `InstalledBuildsContractTest` now, in S1, against the committed capture from SEQ-3, and get it green before S2a exists: per org, the row ORDER as captured (not id order); `name` and `key` compared as raw bytes so the U+2019 in id 1 is pinned; `assertSame(1, $row['pivot']['is_available'])` — an integer, never truthy, never a boolean; `icon.original_url` non-null on every row; the `{status, data}` envelope literal; and never `[]` for an org that has rows. Then S2a's job is to keep a green test green rather than to author its own grader.

verification.corrected_title: Nothing pins /features' row order, envelope keys, name/key bytes or the is_available integer — the only existing coverage is the icon
verification.notes:
Core CONFIRMED, title overstated.

Refuted as literally written: /features is not untested. tests/Feature/MobileMediaBoundaryTest.php:75 (`the_features_endpoint_never_returns_a_null_icon_even_with_no_media`) and :100 (`the_features_endpoint_uses_the_real_icon_when_it_is_present`) both hit `/api/mobile/masjids/{id}/features` and would fail if the icon envelope regressed — which is the 2026-08-28 shape. LegacyFeaturesTelemetryTest::the_payload_is_unchanged_by_being_counted (:162-171) compares a counted response against an uncounted one in the same run, so both move together — it proves the middleware is inert, not that the payload is stable. title: The kill lever has a numbered step with a check; the restore has neither a step nor an ordering constraint against the marker
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/DECISIONS.md:1359-1364 (item 5) and :1410-1420 (deploy notes — kill only); /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Console/Commands/AppMenuRestore.php; server-plan.md §9 (the sequence diagram never mentions the restore). HEAD 4a2a57b.
scenario: S2b night. The operator opens the maintenance window and runs `app-menu:restore` first, because it is the step that undoes the thing they have been living with for three weeks and it feels like the start of the work. `AppMenu::killed()`'s 60-second cache is forgotten by the command, so within a minute `/menu` answers 200 from the switches — while the marker is not in yet, so `/features` is still the pivot. For however long the deploy takes, an R1 MEC TestFlight build (internal or external) cold-launching gets a side menu that lists Qur'an, from an organisation whose legacy list has said Qur'an is off since before the branch existed. That is precisely the divergence item 5 exists to prevent, appearing at the one moment everyone is watching, and it looks like the cutover broke MEC. The reverse ordering error is worse in a different way: if `verify-cutover` finds a difference and the migration is rolled back but the restore has already run, the window stays open until someone remembers to re-kill.
why_it_matters: Item 5 is the load-bearing decision both client lanes are planned around, and its enforcement is entirely in one command being run at the right time. The kill side got promoted from prose to a numbered step with a proof after the author noticed the same class of problem. The restore side is still prose — in fact it is not even prose; §9's sequence diagram does not contain it.
suggested_fix: Add the restore to the S2b runbook as a numbered step explicitly ordered LAST: after `migrate --force`, after `app-features:verify-cutover` prints zero differences, and after the byte- and order-sensitive `/features` diff passes for every captured org. Give it the same prove-it-with-the-endpoint shape (`curl .../masjids/13/menu` must return `"status":"success"` and a hash), and state the rollback rule in the same bullet: if the cutover is rolled back, re-run `app-menu:kill` before anything else.

verification.corrected_title: `app-menu:restore` appears in no runbook and has no ordering constraint against the marker, in either direction
verification.notes:
Core CONFIRMED, scenario wrong in two places.

Confirmed: `grep -n restore DECISIONS.md` returns ZERO hits — app-menu:restore is not in the decision record at all, let alone the deploy notes, and server-plan.md §9's sequence block does not contain it. app/Console/Commands/AppMenuRestore.php exists and works. DECISIONS.md:1354-1358 is item 5 (the finding cites :1359-1364).

Wrong (1): the 60-second-cache detail. Both commands call `Cache::forget(AppMenu::KILL_CACHE_KEY)` immediately after the save (AppMenuKill.php:52, AppMenuRestore.php:40) and the store is the shared database, so a restore bites at once, not "within a minute". The TTL only matters when the row is changed by something other than these commands. Minor, but it is the kind of detail that makes a reader distrust the rest.

Wrong (2): the forward scenario needs a tester holding an R1 build during the S2b window, and §9 states "R1 internal builds are gated on S2b being live on production" — so by the plan's own rule nobody has one yet. Point the finding at the REVERSE direction instead, which needs no such assumption and which the finding already identifies as "worse": the S2b migration is rolled back per §7.3, `down()` deletes the marker so /features reverts to the pivot, but `app-menu:restore` has already been run and nothing re-kills it. /menu then serves MEC's switch-derived menu — which lists Qur'an — against a /features that says Qur'an is off, permanently, until a human remembers a command that is written down nowhere. The suggested fix (restore LAST, after verify-cutover and the byte diff, with "if the cutover is rolled back, re-run app-menu:kill first" in the same bullet) is right as written.

title: `migrate:rollback` un-derives /features but leaves every capability override the cutover wrote — BISS keeps six admin screens its owner had switched off
location: server-plan.md §7.3 item 2 (the literal A2 mapping, "One DB transaction per org that HAS pivot rows") vs item 5 ("`down()` deletes the marker, so the pivot is the source again. Overrides are reversed separately by `app-features:revert-cutover`") and the instruction three sentences later: "Any difference means `down()` first, investigate second." Writer target is /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Http/Controllers/AdminDashboard/MasjidsController.php::setCapability; the invariant it protects is stated at /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Models/Masjid.php:395-400. HEAD 4a2a57b.
scenario: Production facts: org 18 (BISS) has pivot rows ON for ids 6,7,8,9,10,11 while the switches say OFF for all six — the largest disagreement in the fleet. To keep BISS's installed app byte-identical, §7.3 item 2 must write donation_link, about_us, gallery, services, announcements and contact_requests ON. The operator then runs the post-migration byte diff, finds a wrong row somewhere, and follows the runbook: `migrate:rollback`. `down()` deletes the marker, /features reverts to the pivot, and every signal says the cutover is undone. It is not: the six capability overrides are still written. BISS's admins log in the next morning to six admin screens — Announcements, About Us, Gallery, Services, Contact Requests and the donation link — that the owner had deliberately switched off, each one now accepting live content and intake that the next forward attempt will have to reconcile. The same applies to org 16 (IntelliCor), where §7.3 already flags in prose that preserving the pivot "also hands Intellicor's admins those screens" — it just does not say that a rollback leaves them handed over. And once `app-menu:restore` runs, /menu derives from those same overrides, so BISS's side menu lists all six too.
why_it_matters: The rollback instruction and the thing it rolls back are two sentences apart in the same numbered list, and only one of them is in the instruction. `down()` reverses the READ path in one statement; reversing the WRITE path needs a second, differently-named command (`app-features:revert-cutover`) whose existence is mentioned but which the rollback sentence never invokes. Under the pressure of a bad byte diff at 1am, an operator runs the command the runbook names. This is the same silent-success shape as SEQ-5 — the rollback reports done and half of what it undid is still in place — except here the residue is durable data rather than a ten-minute cache.
suggested_fix: Make the rollback one instruction, not two: change §7.3's "Any difference means `down()` first, investigate second" to name both steps in order — `migrate:rollback` THEN `app-features:revert-cutover` THEN `app-menu:kill` if the restore has already run (SEQ-8) — and have `down()` print the exact revert command with the cutover window's timestamps filled in, so the second step cannot be the one nobody remembers. Better still, give `app-features:verify-cutover` a mode that fails loudly while a marker is absent but null-actor ledger rows from a cutover window still stand, so a half-reverted production cannot sit there looking clean.

title: `features.lastgood` is deliberately unreachable by every flush, so a wrong body written at S2b survives the rollback for thirty days with no command able to clear it
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Support/MobileCache.php:168-184 (the `never` clause: "nothing here may forget it") and :202-208 (`flushOwnPayloads` names four keys and "never matches a prefix"); /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/tests/Feature/MobileCacheFamilyFlushTest.php:255-278 pins the exemption; server-plan.md §7.4 writes it inside the `remember` closure with `now()->addDays(30)`. `grep -rn lastgood app/ database/ routes/ config/` returns exactly one hit — the docblock. HEAD 4a2a57b.
scenario: S2b lands. The derivation is subtly wrong for one org — say org 18, where six rows have to be reconstructed from switches the migration just wrote. The first phone to hit /features after `up()`'s flush populates the cache AND writes that wrong body to `features.lastgood` with a thirty-day TTL, because §7.4 writes lastgood unconditionally from whatever the current source produced. The operator spots the difference and rolls back. `down()` restores the pivot; a later flush (a switch flip, a rename, SEQ-5's suggested fix) clears FEATURES. `features.lastgood` is cleared by none of them — by design, and with a test pinning that design. Three weeks later the pivot read fails for a moment (a table lock during the S3a export, a connection blip), the never-5xx chain reaches step 4, and Play vc13 at BISS is served the poisoned body: six rows in the wrong state, tiles shifted in the `take(9)/drop(9)` grid, HTTP 200, one `Log::warning` that reads like the chain working correctly.
why_it_matters: The exemption is right for the failure it was designed against — a flush must not destroy the last-resort answer. But it makes lastgood the only piece of state in this lane that a rollback cannot reach, and §7.4 fills it from the source under test rather than from a source known good. "Last good" is doing work the code does not do: nothing validates the body before storing it, so after the cutover the name is a claim rather than a property. There is no artisan command to inspect or clear it either, so even a human who knows about it has no lever short of writing raw cache rows.
suggested_fix: Two cheap options, either alone is enough. (a) Do not write lastgood from the derived source at all — write it only from `LegacyFeatures::fromPivot()`, so the last-resort answer is always the contract's own reference source and the cutover cannot poison it; the derived body then has the pivot behind it in every direction. (b) If it must mirror whatever was served, give it a generation suffix tied to the marker (`features.lastgood.pre-cutover` / `.post-cutover`), so `down()` selects the pre-cutover one by reverting the source and nothing has to be forgotten. Either way, ship a read-only `app-features:lastgood --org=N` so a human can see what is in there before the day it gets served.

scenario: Deploy night. The operator has two documents. DECISIONS says: run `app-menu:kill` immediately after bin/deploy, before telling anyone, and curl for 404. The plan's production-verification section says: expect /menu to have gone 404 → 200, assert its structure for orgs 1, 5 and 13, check the 304 path, and exercise the kill switch "and restored". Both cannot be done in the order written: the structural asserts need the menu live, and the postcheck ends on `restore`. An operator working from §8.4 — which is the document that actually lists what to curl — finishes with the menu ON, ticks the box that says the kill switch was exercised, and goes to bed. DECISIONS.md:1406 states exactly what that costs: "a deploy that does not run this ships `/menu` LIVE — the opposite of the decision." It then stays live for the three weeks to S2b, because nothing re-checks it and `AppMenu::killed()` fails open in every direction (AppMenu.php:315-330), so no alarm exists. The first client to reach it is whichever R1 build the two lanes are building freely on the assumption the endpoint is dark — and at MEC that menu lists Qur'an, from an organisation whose /features has said Qur'an is off since before this branch existed.
why_it_matters: This is the ordering hazard SEQ-8 identifies at S2b, already present at S1, and with a worse ending: at S2b someone is watching, at S1 the window is three weeks long and unattended. It is also the specific reason SEQ-6's `-o /dev/null` check matters — the one gate that would catch a menu left live is a status code that a missing route also produces, and the postcheck script said to assert it does not exist. The two documents were plainly written at different times; nothing in the repository reconciles them, and item 5 is the decision both client lanes are planned around.
suggested_fix: Write the S1 postcheck as one ordered list in one place, with the kill LAST and proved by the body: (1) curl /menu for 13 and assert 200 plus the payload hash — this is what proves route:cache took, and it is the assertion SEQ-6 wants; (2) the structural asserts for 1, 5, 13 and the 304 path; (3) `app-menu:kill`; (4) curl /menu for 13 and grep the body for `"status":"failed"` and a `data` object, which only AppMenuController::unavailable() at :170-178 produces. Then delete §8.4's "the kill switch exercised and restored" phrasing, because ending on `restored` is the bug. Add a weekly `tenancy:canary`-style assertion, or one line in the existing hourly canary, that /menu still 404s through the window — the kill row fails open by design, so nothing else will ever tell you it stopped biting.
ft: The S1 runbook and the S1 postcheck give contradictory orders about the kill row, and following the postcheck leaves /menu live for the whole S1→S2b window
notes: verifier-raised

title: Three lenses assert a 30-day `features.lastgood` landmine; §7.4's own code refutes them, and the real defect points the other way
location: server-plan.md §7.4 — `Cache::put(masjidKey($id,'features.lastgood'), $rows, now()->addDays(30))` sits INSIDE the `Cache::remember` closure. Against BI-V1, OB-3 and SEQ-M2, which all describe a poisoned entry surviving a rollback for thirty days; and N5-03, which correctly refutes them.
scenario: The contradiction has to be settled before anyone writes LegacyFeatures, because the two models imply opposite fixes. The put is inside the closure, so it fires on every FEATURES cache miss — at least every 600 seconds under any traffic — and it fires only when `rows()` returned without throwing. So a wrong-but-successful body is overwritten by the next successful build, and `down()` deleting the marker means the very next miss rewrites lastgood from the pivot. BI-V1's "thirty days later a DB blip serves a body written during a deploy that was rolled back a month earlier" cannot happen to an org with traffic, and an org without traffic never reads lastgood either. What IS true, and what none of the three framings says, is the mirror image: lastgood holds the last answer that did not throw, never a known-good one, and because it is rewritten on every successful miss, the first successful post-cutover read destroys the last pivot-derived copy. From that moment there is no pre-cutover floor anywhere in the system — the four-step chain's last resort and its first step are derived from the same switches. A derivation that is wrong for org 14 is equally wrong at step 1 and at step 3.
why_it_matters: An implementer reading BI-V1/OB-3/SEQ-M2 builds a flush command and a fingerprint-versioned key to defuse a landmine that defuses itself, and leaves the actual hole open. The actual hole is that the never-fail chain has no independent source: three of its four steps read the same switches, and the fourth (the capture) does not exist yet.
suggested_fix: Take SEQ-M2's option (a), which is the only proposal in the set that survives this reading: until S3a, write `features.lastgood` only from `LegacyFeatures::fromPivot($masjid)`, never from the derived path. The pivot lives until S3a and is the contract's own reference source, so the last resort is then genuinely independent of the thing under test. Keep MobileCache's never-flush rule exactly as it is. Strike the 30-day-persistence framing from the record so nobody implements against it.
ft: Three lenses assert a 30-day `features.lastgood` landmine; §7.4's own code refutes them, and the real defect points the other way
notes: critic

title: Org 17 is invisible to all three cutover gates at once, and §8.2 pre-commits the answer §7.4 says the owner must give
location: server-plan.md §7.4 ("conflict (c), owner-resolved per org; OQ-5") against §8.2's `MobileAppFeaturesRetiredTest` ("a newly provisioned org's `/features` still answers 11 rows from type defaults"); AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:233-240 (class (c), `blocking: false`, `key: null`); the scratchpad capture has eight `features-org-*.json` and no org-17 body.
scenario: Org 17's `/features` goes from `{"status":"success","data":[]}` to eleven rows at the marker — the plan's own words call this "the only change installed apps see". Now count what could catch it. (1) The committed capture: §7.1 names org 17 in its list, and the capture as taken skips it, because a script that saves bodies for orgs with rows has nothing to save. (2) `app-features:verify-cutover`: §7.3 has it diff pivot value against derived value per org and id — org 17 has no pivot rows, so the comparison is vacuous and prints zero differences truthfully. (3) The plan command: class (c) is raised with `blocking: false` and `key: null`, so it cannot block and `config/app_feature_cutover.php` (keyed org → key → decision) cannot express an answer for it. Three independent gates, all inoperative, on the one org the plan admits is changing. Meanwhile §7.4 says the outcome is owner-resolved and §8.2 writes a test asserting it is eleven rows — the test answers the question the plan reserves for the owner. Nobody is hurt today (org 17 is the QA sandbox, `app_version_settings: []`, no build points at it), but §7.5 deletes the provisioning pivot writes, so every organisation created after S2b is exactly this shape, with exactly these three blind gates.
why_it_matters: The blast radius is zero now and total later. The first real masjid provisioned after S2b inherits an endpoint whose correct answer was decided by a test rather than by the owner, verified by a comparison that is vacuous for it, against a golden that has no entry for it. Byte-identity is the branch's whole promise and this is the single documented exception to it — exceptions are exactly what needs a gate.
suggested_fix: Three cheap pieces, all before S2b. Capture org 17's empty body explicitly into the fixtures so the golden records `[]` rather than omitting it. Give class (c) a resolvable org-level key (`17 => ['_no_rows' => 'serve_defaults'|'serve_empty']`), make it blocking while unresolved, and stop printing "No decision is outstanding" while a class-(c) notice stands. Then reconcile §7.4 and §8.2: either the owner decides and the test asserts whatever they decided, or the plan drops "owner-resolved" and says eleven rows is the standing decision — but not both.
ft: Org 17 is invisible to all three cutover gates at once, and §8.2 pre-commits the answer §7.4 says the owner must give
notes: critic

title: Five lenses found the ON-direction blindness and split 2-3 on severity; §7.3's prose names the org with NULL overrides and omits the org with four explicit reversals
location: AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:259 (`if ($pivotValue !== false) { continue; }`) and :254-256 (the side_effect ternary); server-plan.md §7.3's closing paragraph names Intellicor only; §8.2's `CutoverMigrationTest` variants are all-on / school six / mixed off / no rows / donate off with a live subscription / MAS Youth — none is "pivot ON over an explicit false override".
scenario: BI-4, N5-06, cw-3, R-M1 and OB-7 are the same defect found five times, rated must_fix twice and should_fix three times. The split is resolvable and both halves are right about different things: the WRITES are benign for phones (an ON-ward write is precisely what preserves byte-identity — should_fix), while the REPORT is actively wrong (every one of those rows prints "Also means: None: nothing is switched off." beside a column that says `contact_requests=true` — must_fix on its own terms, because the artefact the owner signs is the artefact that lies). What none of the five says is that the plan names the wrong example. §7.3's only acknowledgement is "preserving Intellicor's pivot writes `services=true` and `donation_link=true`, which also hands Intellicor's admins those screens" — and I confirmed on production that org 16 has `capability_overrides = NULL`, so Intellicor's case is the mildest instance in the fleet: two org-type defaults, no recorded decision reversed. The org with four explicit `false` overrides being reversed — org 18 BISS (about_us, gallery, announcements, contact_requests, set by user 1 on 2026-09-14, and the only org besides 13 with any overrides at all) — appears nowhere in §7.3, produces zero findings, and is omitted entirely by `--conflicts-only`. A BISS parent sends a message into a contact form the school closed on purpose, gets a success confirmation, and nobody is watching that inbox.
why_it_matters: Five independent lenses converging is the strongest signal in this whole review, and the plan's one-sentence nod to it picks the example that makes it look like a rounding error. There is also no test slot: §8.2's six `CutoverMigrationTest` variants all exercise pivot-OFF rows, so the direction that accounts for twelve of the thirteen production differences is untested as well as unreported.
suggested_fix: Adopt the class (e) all five lenses converged on — pivot ON while the derived value is OFF — blocking when the key is explicitly present as `false` in `capability_overrides`, a notice when it merely grants an org-type default (that split is exactly the 4-vs-2 shape org 18 has). Compute the side_effect column from the DIRECTION of the write so a row that flips a switch can never read "nothing is switched off", with an ON-direction sentence per key (`contact_requests`: "PUBLIC INTAKE RE-OPENS"). Key `--conflicts-only` off `agrees === false` as well as findings. Rewrite §7.3's paragraph around BISS rather than Intellicor, and add the seventh `CutoverMigrationTest` variant.
ft: Five lenses found the ON-direction blindness and split 2-3 on severity; §7.3's prose names the org with NULL overrides and omits the org with four explicit reversals
notes: critic

title: legacyAvailability special-cases id 10 ahead of the registry, so the config can no longer move it
location: app/Support/AppMenu.php legacyAvailability(): `if ($legacyId === 10) { return ! $org->moduleIsOff('announcements'); }` before the registry loop
scenario: An operator edits config/app_menu.php so that the `announcements` item's `any_of` no longer names the `announcements` module (say a rename to `news`). registry() validates and accepts it, /menu follows the new key, but legacyAvailability(10) keeps reading the hard-coded string and quietly disagrees with the menu it is supposed to be the fallback for. Also: the method's documented "an id the registry does not know fails OPEN" return is unreachable, because validate() requires legacy ids 1..11 exactly once and otherwise falls back to DEFAULT_REGISTRY.
why_it_matters: Low likelihood, but it makes the registry a partial source of truth precisely for the one id whose asymmetry the docblock is at pains to explain, and it means a MenuLegacyParityTest (§8.2) could pass against a config the two readers interpret differently.
suggested_fix: Express the asymmetry in the registry instead of in code — e.g. give the announcements item a `legacy_any_of => ['announcements']` alongside its `any_of => ['announcements','events']` — and have legacyAvailability prefer `legacy_any_of` when present. Then delete the id-10 special case and the unreachable fail-open return, or add a test that reaches it.

verification.corrected_title: The id-10 special case sits ahead of the registry, and legacyAvailability's fail-open return is dead code
verification.notes:
The code reading is right: legacyAvailability() at AppMenu.php:440-453 checks `if ($legacyId === 10) return ! $org->moduleIsOff('announcements');` before the registry loop.

The stated SCENARIO is refuted. validate() at :258-262 rejects any `any_of` entry that is not in Masjid::MODULE_KEYS, so renaming the announcements item's any_of to `news` makes registry() log a warning and return DEFAULT_REGISTRY — both readers then agree and nothing drifts. The drift needs a rename to a DIFFERENT REAL module key (say announcements → any_of ['programs']), at which point /menu follows programs while legacyAvailability(10) still reads announcements. That variant works, so the core survives; the example does not.

The dead-code half is confirmed and is the more useful part: `grep -rn legacyAvailability app tests config routes database` returns exactly one caller, AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:244, iterating LEGACY_MAP's keys 1..11, and validate() guarantees the registry holds each of 1..11 exactly once — so the `return true` at :452 is unreachable from every caller that exists, and no test calls the method directly at all. Either reach it or delete it.

nit is the right rating.

title: The last-resort floor lives in a config file — the one thing bin/deploy guarantees is stale — and has no entry for org 17 or for any org created after the capture
location: server-plan.md §7.1 and §7.4 (`config/legacy_features_capture.php`, `LegacyFeatures::fromCapture`); compare app/Models/Masjid.php:350 (MODULE_DEFAULTS) and app/Support/AppMenu.php:70 (DEFAULT_REGISTRY), both code copies for exactly this reason
scenario: Two separate holes. (1) Deploy window: the capture file is new, so between `git merge` and `config:clear` at bin/deploy:209 `config('legacy_features_capture')` is null. On the S2b deploy that window overlaps the moment the migration has already inserted the marker and flushFamily'd every org, so `/features` is deriving COLD with no metadata source; the derived rows carry name, key, created_at, updated_at and row order from the capture, and Play vc13 routes BY NAME. A phone that launches in that window either gets rows with null names that route nowhere, or (if the lookup throws) falls through to the pivot. (2) Coverage: the committed capture has fixtures for orgs 1, 2, 5, 13, 14, 16, 18, 19 — there is NO fixture for org 17, and none can exist for any organisation provisioned after 2026-09-16. §7.4 says orgs with no pivot rows "return the 11 rows in Burlington's captured order", which only works if `fromCapture` has a catalogue-level default rather than a per-org lookup; a per-org lookup returns nothing for 17 and for every future org, which lands back in N5-02.
why_it_matters: This branch already establishes, in two docblocks that name bin/deploy by name, that anything which must answer correctly during a deploy has to be a code copy. The one payload with a never-fail promise is the one that was made a config file instead.
suggested_fix: Generate the capture as a `const` array on `LegacyFeatures` (committed, mirrored by a test against config/, exactly like AppMenuRegistryMirrorTest does for the registry), with `config()` allowed only to override it. Give it an explicit CATALOGUE default (Burlington's captured 11 rows and order) used for any org id it does not know, and pin that with a test that asks for org 17 and for an id that has never existed.

verification.corrected_title: Prefer a committed const over config/legacy_features_capture.php for the last-resort floor — both named failure scenarios do not hold
verification.notes:
Both concrete scenarios fail.

(1) Deploy window. The capture config ships in the S2a deploy (§7.2: 'Ships: app/Support/LegacyFeatures.php, ... config/legacy_features_capture.php'), which is a SEPARATE, EARLIER release than S2b (§7.3). By the time the S2b migration inserts the marker, bootstrap/cache/config.php has already been rebuilt at the end of the S2a deploy, so there is no 'deriving COLD with no metadata source' window at S2b. Within the S2a window itself the marker is absent by design, so /features still reads the pivot and the capture is only fallback step 4 — reachable only after the derivation AND the pivot read have both thrown, inside a ~90-second window.

(2) Coverage. §7.1 explicitly names org 17 in the capture set ('at least 1, 2, 5, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19'), and §7.4 already specifies the catalogue-level default the finding asks for ('Orgs with no pivot rows today return the 11 rows in Burlington's captured order'). The finding asserts the contents of config/legacy_features_capture.php, which does not exist at HEAD — grep across app/, config/, routes/, database/ and tests/ returns nothing for legacy_features_capture. The eight-org fixture set it describes matches this review's own /private/tmp capture directory, not the plan's committed capture.

KEPT AS A NIT: the underlying preference is sound and consistent with the branch's own precedent — AppMenu::DEFAULT_REGISTRY and Masjid::MODULE_KEYS/MODULE_DEFAULTS are code copies with mirror tests for exactly this reason, and the payload with the strongest promise is the one held in a config file. Worth doing when LegacyFeatures is written; not a defect at HEAD.

title: Every /features failure path bypasses the cache, so a sustained fault turns a 10-minute-cached endpoint into an uncached one on a 1-vCPU box
location: server-plan.md §7.4 — the catch blocks sit outside Cache::remember and none of the three fallbacks writes the FEATURES key
scenario: Once the derived path is failing, the endpoint stops being cached at all: each request re-enters `Cache::remember` (miss), rebuilds, throws, then runs `LegacyFeatures::fromPivot()` — `Masjid::with('features.icon')->find()`, three queries plus the throttle's own database-cache round trips — and discards the result. Production is nproc=1, pm.max_children=12, CACHE_STORE=database, SESSION_DRIVER=database, QUEUE_CONNECTION=database, all on the same MariaDB. A fault that lasts through an adhan-time launch burst (the one moment /features traffic is bursty — today's peak is 18/min but that is with one shipped app; the cost is per-launch, not per-10-min-per-org) turns the recovery path into the load. It is the moment the box is already unhealthy that the endpoint chooses to stop caching.
why_it_matters: The fallback chain is designed to make the fault invisible to handsets; as written it makes the fault maximally expensive to the server, which is how an org-level problem becomes a site-level one.
suggested_fix: Cache the fallback result too, under the same FEATURES key with a short TTL (60 s) and a marker saying which step produced it, so a fault costs one build per org per minute rather than one per launch. Assert it in LegacyFeaturesNeverFailsTest: two requests during a forced fault must produce one derivation attempt, not two.

verification.corrected_title: Fallback answers are not cached — a design trade, not a defect, and the proposed fix contradicts the rule /menu states for itself
verification.notes:
CONFIRMED structurally: in the §7.4 sketch the catches sit outside Cache::remember and no fallback writes the FEATURES key, so a sustained derivation fault means every request re-enters remember, misses, rebuilds and throws.

CORRECTED on both the severity and the fix.
- The load argument does not survive the reviewer's own numbers, quoted in their checked_ok list: 156 /features hits on 15 Sep, peak 18 in one minute. Four extra database-cache round trips plus `Masjid::with('features.icon')->find()` at 18/min on a box that already serves the whole launch tuple is not how an org-level fault becomes a site-level one.
- More importantly the suggested fix conflicts with a principle this branch states and tests elsewhere. AppMenuController deliberately lets a throwing payload build propagate out of Cache::remember so that nothing is cached, and the reviewer's own checked_ok credits that: 'a throwing payload build caches nothing ... so a failed build cannot be served for the TTL on /menu'. Caching a degraded /features answer under the live FEATURES key is the thing /menu refuses to do. A short-TTL entry tagged with the step that produced it might still be worth having, but it is a trade to argue, not a defect to fix.

Downgraded to nit. The one part worth keeping verbatim is the test assertion: two requests during a forced fault should not mean two derivation attempts.

title: "/features and activated_features can never disagree" is not achievable: one is cached for ten minutes with a 30-day floor, the other is uncached
location: server-plan.md §7.4 last paragraph; app/Http/Controllers/Api/V1/SettingController.php:22-39 (init() is an uncached findOrFail) and :81-90 (activated_features); app/Support/MobileCache.php:170-178
scenario: Sharing `LegacyFeatures::activated()` makes the DERIVATION identical; it cannot make the ANSWERS identical, because the two endpoints have different caching. `/v1/settings` reads the database on every request. `/features` serves a 10-minute cached entry and, when the chain falls through, a `features.lastgood` entry that flushFamily is explicitly forbidden from forgetting. Sequence: a SuperAdmin switches Donate off at MEC (13); setCapability flushes FEATURES correctly; the derivation then fails for any of the reasons above; the iPhone's launch tuple asks both endpoints in the same second and gets `/features` with Donate present (from lastgood) and `/v1/settings` with Donate absent from activated_features. The member sees a Donate tile in the drawer for a screen the settings payload says does not exist. Separately, `/v1/settings` today cannot fail on this field at all (it is a pure collection filter over an eager-loaded relation); after the cutover it gains every failure mode the derivation has, on the endpoint that also carries prayer times, iqama, theme and jumaa — a strictly worse blast radius than /features, and §7.4's code sketch only guards the features controller.
why_it_matters: The stated reason for sharing the derivation is a guarantee the architecture cannot deliver, so the team will stop looking for the disagreement it was meant to rule out — and the launch endpoint quietly inherits a new class of failure.
suggested_fix: Either have SettingController read the same cached FEATURES entry (one source, one cache, one fallback state) or drop the "can never disagree" sentence and write down which endpoint wins and for how long. Whichever way, wrap activated_features in its own fallback with the same four steps, and extend the §8.2 test to assert both endpoints agree while each of the four steps is forced.

verification.corrected_title: "/features and activated_features can never disagree" overstates what a shared derivation buys — the two endpoints have different caching
verification.notes:
CONFIRMED on the wording point, which is fair and worth fixing in the plan. Api/V1/SettingController::init() (:22-39) is an uncached findOrFail with eager loads, and activated_features (:81-90) is a pure collection filter over `features.icon`; /features is a 10-minute Cache::remember entry with a 30-day lastgood floor that flushFamily may not forget. Sharing LegacyFeatures::activated() makes the DERIVATION identical and cannot make the ANSWERS identical. Rewrite the sentence, or say which endpoint wins and for how long.

CORRECTED on three claims.
- '§7.4's code sketch only guards the features controller' is contradicted by §7.4's own next paragraph: activated_features is 'derived by the same LegacyFeatures::activated($masjid) WITH THE SAME FALLBACK CHAIN and the same order'. Only the illustrative code block is features-only; the plan already says the chain applies to both.
- The named client is wrong. §7.4 calls /v1/settings 'the web payload'; it is keyed off a `masjid-id` HEADER, not the {masjid_id} route the mobile endpoints use, and nothing in this branch or the plan puts it in an iPhone launch tuple. 'The iPhone's launch tuple asks both endpoints in the same second' is not established, so the member-sees-a-Donate-tile scenario has no verified client.
- The disagreement is not created by the cutover. Cached /features versus uncached /v1/settings already diverges for up to ten minutes on main whenever a pivot row changes without a flush.

title: The /features route is not whereNumber-constrained, so aliased ids are served as org 1 and counted as Burlington launches
location: routes/api.php:145-150 (no ->whereNumber('masjid_id'); the member routes at :177, :218 and :229 have it); app/Http/Middleware/CountLegacyFeaturesHit.php:96-102
scenario: `GET /api/mobile/masjids/1abc/features` reaches `Masjid::findOrFail('1abc')`, and MariaDB coerces the string in `WHERE id = '1abc'` to 1 — so it serves Burlington's list with a 200. The middleware then does `(int) '1abc'` and increments `mobile.telemetry.features.<date>.1.untagged`. Same for `0001`, `1 `, `1.0`. The docblock's stated defence — refusals are not counted, so "one looping scanner" cannot "look like a stranded congregation" — only covers 404s; the aliasing path produces a 200 and is counted. A crawler or an uptime monitor pointed at a padded id reads as untagged Burlington traffic, which is the exact number S3b is gated on, and it keeps the endpoint undeletable indefinitely.
why_it_matters: The counter exists to answer one question — may we delete this endpoint — and this is a way for a stranger to make the answer permanently no, with no error anywhere.
suggested_fix: Add `->whereNumber('masjid_id')` to the features prefix (the pattern the member routes already use and whose docblock at :168 calls load-bearing). That also makes the 404 for a garbage id honest, which is what the telemetry test at LegacyFeaturesTelemetryTest:136 assumes.

verification.notes:
CONFIRMED, and verified against live production rather than inferred. `GET /api/mobile/masjids/1abc/features`, `/01/features` and `/0001/features` each return HTTP 200 with Burlington's eleven rows and pivot.masjid_id = 1 — MySQL coerces the string in `WHERE id = '1abc'` to 1, so findOrFail resolves. routes/api.php:145-150 has no ->whereNumber('masjid_id') while the member prefixes at :177, :218 and :229 do, under a comment at :168 that calls whereNumber load-bearing. CountLegacyFeaturesHit.php:96-102 then does `(int) $org` and increments mobile.telemetry.features.<date>.1.untagged, and the docblock's stated defence ('refusals are not counted') genuinely only covers 404s, because this path is a 200.

Two corrections, neither of which changes the rating. It does NOT multiply throttle buckets: RateLimiter::for('mobile') (AppServiceProvider.php:708-725) keys on device id and IP, never on the masjid, so the routes/family.php 'three different doors' concern does not transfer here. And it cannot serve the wrong organisation's list, because the cache key `(int) $masjid_id` and MySQL's coercion agree on the same id — there is no cross-tenant read or cache poisoning.

So the impact is exactly telemetry integrity on the counter S3b is gated on, which is what a nit is for. The one-line fix is right and also makes LegacyFeaturesTelemetryTest:136's 404 assumption honest.

title: The S2 contract test masks the icon object wholesale, which also masks its key set — the field most likely to change shape
location: server-plan.md §8.2 LegacyFeaturesContractTest ("byte- and order-identical per org with the `icon` object masked (media ids and host differ in CI) and the icon asserted non-null separately"); app/Support/MobileMedia.php:69-88
scenario: Production serves a full ~20-key Spatie media row per icon (id, uuid, model_type, collection_name, mime_type, size, order_column, created_at, updated_at, original_url, preview_url, …), confirmed in the capture for org 1. `MobileMedia::envelope`'s fallback path returns a THREE-key object {id, original_url, preview_url} — its own comment says "`id` is the only field an older non-optional model requires", which is a guess about the iOS model, not a pinned fact. Masking `icon` to paper over volatile VALUES also hides a change in the key SET. If the derived path emits the lean shape for a row whose media is missing, and the iPhone's icon struct has any non-optional field beyond id, Codable fails on the whole array and the drawer is empty — and CI is green, because the test masked exactly that object.
why_it_matters: The 2026-08-28 incident was one null icon in this payload emptying the drawer on every phone. The contract test written to make that unrepeatable excludes the icon from the byte comparison.
suggested_fix: Mask the volatile VALUES, not the object: assert the icon's key set matches the capture exactly, and normalise id/uuid/host/timestamps before comparing. Add one case that forces the media row missing and asserts the emitted key set against whatever the shipped iOS model actually requires (get that from the ios-plan lane rather than inferring it).

verification.notes:
CONFIRMED on the facts. The production capture for org 1 carries a 21-key icon object per row (id, model_type, model_id, uuid, collection_name, name, file_name, mime_type, disk, conversions_disk, size, manipulations, custom_properties, generated_conversions, responsive_images, order_column, created_at, updated_at, original_url, preview_url — plus model_id). MobileMedia::envelope's fallback branch (app/Support/MobileMedia.php:80-88) returns three keys, and its own comment concedes the guess: 'id is the only field an older non-optional model requires'. §8.2's LegacyFeaturesContractTest as specified masks the whole `icon` object, so a change in the key SET passes.

Two qualifications. The shape asymmetry is on main, not introduced by this branch — the /features controller is byte-identical to main (`git diff main` on MasjidMobileAppFeaturesController is empty), so this is a gap in a test that does not exist yet rather than a regression. And the plan does already assert the icon non-null separately, so the ask narrows to: assert the key set against the capture and normalise id/uuid/host/timestamps before comparing, plus one case that forces the media row missing. That is the right ask, and the 2026-08-28 precedent justifies it. nit is the correct rating.

title: The "read-only" cutover plan can make outbound Stripe API calls and write warning lines into the post-deploy log sweep
location: app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:280 and :347 (givingEvidence) -> app/Support/GivingSwitch.php:63-67 (liveSubscriptionCount) -> :87-106 (billedAfterCancelCount) -> app/Services/Stripe/DonationService.php:989-1011 (stripeStatusOf) -> :1014-1020 (subscriptions->retrieve)
scenario: As soon as any organisation's legacy id 6 (Donate) is OFF in the pivot, both writesFor() (:347) and the class (b) check (:280) call givingEvidence(), which calls GivingSwitch::liveSubscriptionCount(), which calls billedAfterCancelCount(), which issues one live Stripe subscriptions->retrieve per candidate DonationSubscription on the connected account. An operator running the plan on production per §8.3 step 9 therefore makes outbound third-party API calls from a command whose docblock says "IT WRITES NOTHING, AND SAYS SO OUT LOUD". stripeStatusOf() catches Throwable, so it cannot abort the run — but it writes Log::warning('Could not read subscription status from Stripe.') on every failure, and §8.3 step 12 is a LOG_LEVEL=warning sweep whose stated expectation is "the only new lines should be the ledger warnings from step 5". Stripe warnings appearing in that sweep read as deploy fallout. Note this cannot fire on today's data: I read every pivot row on production and no organisation has id 6 OFF (the only is_available=0 rows anywhere are org 13 feature 1 and orgs 14/16/18/19 features 1-5), so the path is latent, not live. It goes live the first time an org's Donate row is switched off before the cutover, and givingEvidence is called twice per such org (once at :280, once at :347), doubling the calls.
why_it_matters: "Read-only" in this command's docblock means "writes no row in our database", which is true and is what assertWroteNothing measures. It does not mean "has no side effects outside this box", and an operator reading the docblock before running it on production would reasonably assume it did. Outbound calls are also slow and rate-limitable on a command already doing per-org N+1 reads, which lengthens the window in which N5V-M1 can fire.
suggested_fix: Memoise givingEvidence() per organisation so the two call sites cost one evaluation, and give the command a --no-stripe (or --offline) mode that reports giving evidence from local rows only and says in the output that the Stripe-confirmed count was skipped. Say in the class docblock that the giving check reaches Stripe, so the §8.3 step 12 sweep expects those warning lines.
ft: The "read-only" cutover plan can make outbound Stripe API calls and write warning lines into the post-deploy log sweep
notes: verifier-raised

title: Nothing links the plan the owner approved to the writes the migration makes; an org created in between is written unreviewed
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:326-352 (writesFor, the approved specification) vs server-plan.md 7.3 step 2 (the migration recomputes) @ 4a2a57b
scenario:
writesFor() produces the 'Would write' column the owner signs off on, and --json can emit it, but nothing consumes that output: the migration recomputes from a fresh read at bin/deploy:207, days or weeks later. There is no test and no committed artifact asserting 'the migration wrote exactly what the plan printed'.

The gap has teeth because the Mobile App Features admin screen and the onboarding wizard's pivot writes stay live until S2b (section 7.5 deletes them in that same deploy). Onboard a new school on 2026-09-25, after the plan run: it gets the school bundle (11 pivot rows, 6-11 ON) and is migrated silently, in a plan nobody read. Worse, if that school carries any blocking (a) or (b) condition -- a Donate row someone switched off with a donation link already set, say -- the migration's step-1 gate throws at line 207, AFTER the S2b code is on the box. The deleted routes and deleted SPA views (section 7.5) are already live, so the operator cannot open Mobile App Features to inspect or fix the pivot row that is blocking them. Installed apps stay correct (the marker is absent, /features still reads the pivot), but the cutover is stuck with its own admin screen removed.

Separately: a SuperAdmin editing the pivot between the plan run and the migration silently invalidates the resolutions in config/app_feature_cutover.php, which were decided against the older pivot, and nothing notices.
why_it_matters: A plan computed from a snapshot and applied later is a race, and the only thing standing between it and a wrong write is that the migration happens to recompute. Recomputing means the artifact the owner approved and the artifact that ships are different objects with no equality check.
suggested_fix: Commit the plan's --json output as a signed manifest (org id, legacy id, key, value) alongside config/app_feature_cutover.php, and have the migration compare its freshly computed writes against it: any org present in one and not the other, or any differing value, throws and names the org -- BEFORE any write and before the S2b deletions take effect. Move the section 7.5 route/SPA deletions into a separate deploy after the migration has succeeded, so a refusal never strands the operator without the screen.

verification.notes:
The observation is accurate as far as it goes: writesFor() produces the approved column, --json can emit it, nothing consumes it, and server-plan.md 7.3 step 2 has the migration recompute from a fresh read. There is no manifest and no equality check.

BUT THE TEETH ARE LARGELY GONE ON INSPECTION. (1) The stranded-operator scenario is REFUTED. bin/deploy is `set -euo pipefail` (:45), so a throwing migration at :207 aborts before config:clear/route:clear/config:cache/route:cache at :210-:214. The previous route cache stays live -- I confirmed routes-v7.php is on the production box, 890703 bytes, Sep 15 16:11 -- so the deleted Mobile App Features routes would still resolve from it and the operator would NOT be locked out of the screen. The stale route cache protects here rather than harming. (2) 7.3 step 1 has the migration re-run the plan and refuse on any unresolved conflict, so a newly onboarded org carrying a blocking (a) or (b) is caught and throws before any write. (3) An org onboarded in between with no blocking conflict is migrated unreviewed, but its writes are the literal pivot mapping, which preserves its own /features exactly; the residual harm is the pinning and provenance already covered by cw-3 and by my missed finding m-2. (4) The "a SuperAdmin edits the pivot and silently invalidates the resolutions" half is real but mild, and cw-2 shows the resolutions are not readable on a cached box anyway.

Downgraded to nit: a process observation worth a line in the runbook (re-run the plan immediately before the deploy), not a defect. The suggestion to move the 7.5 route/SPA deletions into a separate deploy after the migration succeeds is still good hygiene independent of this.

title: givingEvidence() runs twice per organisation on the Donate-off path and can reach Stripe both times
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:347 (inside writesFor, called from :245) and :280 (in planFor) @ 4a2a57b
scenario:
For an org whose id 6 pivot is false, planFor calls writesFor at :245, which evaluates givingEvidence at :347; planFor then evaluates it again at :280 for the (b) finding. givingEvidence calls GivingSwitch::liveSubscriptionCount, which calls billedAfterCancelCount, which for any linked subscription booked after its cancel calls DonationService::stripeStatusOf per candidate -- a live Stripe API call. So a plan run on production makes up to two independent rounds of Stripe reads per affected org, from a command whose whole selling point is that it is safe to run on production.

The two reads can disagree, and the disagreement is not symmetric: GivingSwitch's docblock says that when Stripe cannot be asked the candidate COUNTS, "because refusing a switch-off is the safe mistake". So a single transient Stripe failure on the second call, with the first having succeeded, produces a report where the table says `donation_link=false, giving=false` and the finding underneath says giving is blocked and untouched -- the same contradiction as m-1, arrived at by a different route and without anyone having resolved anything.

Not reachable on production today: writesFor returns early at :338-340 for `$pivotValue === true`, and every org with pivot rows has id 6 ON (verified in the capture), so givingEvidence is never called on any current org and no Stripe call is made by a plan run today.
why_it_matters: A read-only production command should be cheap and self-consistent. Evaluating the same money-critical predicate twice per org costs Stripe round trips nobody budgeted for and lets one report state two different answers to the same question.
suggested_fix: Compute `$giving = $this->givingEvidence($org)` once per org in planFor before the id loop and pass it into writesFor, so the report's finding and its write column are derived from a single observation. A memoised per-org cache on the command instance would do as well and is a two-line change.

title: The branch's only ordered derivation emits section order, not feature_id order — reusing it for the derived /features reshuffles the whole Android grid
location: config/app_menu.php:56-62 and app/Support/AppMenu.php:73-78, 341-364 (visibleItems) @ 4a2a57b
scenario: AppMenu::visibleItems() walks registry['sections'] in order, which flattens to legacy ids [10, 9, 6, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11]. Production serves [1..11] (fixtures/features-org-1.json). AppMenu is already the class the plan command calls for legacy questions (AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:246 calls AppMenu::legacyAvailability), so it is the obvious thing S2a's LegacyFeatures::rows() reuses — and §7.4's requirement that row order come from the capture "not id order" is a sentence in a scratchpad, not a constraint in code. If that reuse happens, Play vc13 on Burlington (org 1, all 11 available) filters to available, draws features.take(9) as a 3x3 grid and features.drop(9).first() full-width, and never draws the 11th at all (git show 8579eee:.../MainMenu.kt:118-139). Today the grid is Qur'an…Services and the full-width row under it is Announcements. Under section order the grid becomes Announcements, Services, Donate, Qur'an, Hadith, Adhkar, Qibla, Tasbih, About Us and the full-width row becomes Gallery. Qur'an moves from the top-left tile to position 4, Announcements jumps to the top-left, and Gallery replaces Announcements at the bottom. No error is raised anywhere — not on the phone, not in laravel.log, not in any test in this branch.
why_it_matters: Row order is a contract only one of the three clients reads positionally, and it is the one that cannot be updated remotely. It is also the contract that is easiest to break by writing the obviously correct code.
suggested_fix: Make the order explicit and hostile to reuse: have LegacyFeatures::rows() iterate the committed capture's order (OB-1) rather than the registry, and add an assertion in AppMenuRegistryMirrorTest that registry section order is NOT equal to legacy-id order — so anybody who wires the two together trips a test that names the reason.

verification.corrected_title: Section order and legacy-id order differ and no test says so — worth an assertion, but nothing at HEAD emits section order into a legacy payload
verification.notes:
THE FACT IS TRUE: config/app_menu.php:56-60 flattens to legacy ids [10,9,6,1,2,3,4,5,7,8,11] and visibleItems() (AppMenu.php:341-364) walks sections in that order. Production serves 1..11. AppMenuRegistryMirrorTest asserts the eleven ids each appear once (`assertSame(range(1,11), $ids)` after sorting) but never that section order differs from id order.

REFUTING EVIDENCE the finding does not engage with:
(1) visibleItems() is not the legacy bridge and cannot be. It returns {key, section, legacy_feature_id, parts} — none of the fields a /features row needs (id, name, key, created_at, updated_at, pivot, icon). Reusing it would be a rewrite, not a reuse.
(2) The actual bridge already exists and is id-keyed: AppMenu::legacyAvailability() (AppMenu.php:440-451), whose own docblock says 'The bridge S2's derived /features reads'.
