title: Retirement removes the only lever that hides an app row without also taking an admin screen away — and that loss is not recorded anywhere
location: plan §7.5 (deletion of the SuperAdmin Mobile App Features screen); keys at /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/config/capabilities.php:158 announcements, :174 about_us, :182 gallery, :198 contact_requests, :271 services, :279 donation_link; consequences enumerated at app/Console/Commands/AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:138-148; HEAD 4a2a57b
scenario: BISS (org 18) is the worst case: 6 of its 11 rows differ between pivot and switches. Today a SuperAdmin can turn Gallery off in the app drawer and BISS staff keep the gallery editor; they can turn Contact Us off in the app and the website's contact form keeps taking messages. After S2b the only remaining lever is capability:gallery / capability:contact_requests, and the command's own SIDE_EFFECTS text says what that costs: the editor is hidden from the org's admins and, for contact_requests, 'PUBLIC INTAKE CLOSES'. So the day after retirement, the answer to 'take Services off the BISS app but leave the editor' is: you can't any more. Nobody sees an error — the capability simply no longer exists as a separable thing.
why_it_matters: This is a permanent product capability being deleted, not a refactor. The plan surfaces the conflicts once, at cutover, and never states that the separation itself is gone forever. That is an owner decision, and DECISIONS.md does not contain it.
suggested_fix: Either get the owner to sign this off explicitly in DECISIONS.md as an accepted loss, or keep an app-only visibility override in the app_feature_cutovers table (key → hidden_in_app) that LegacyFeatures and AppMenu both honour, so a row can still be removed from the drawer without touching the admin module.

verification.corrected_title: The separability loss is recorded only as a rejected alternative, not as a named consequence, in the new DECISIONS.md entry
verification.notes:
CAPABILITY FACTS CONFIRMED EXACTLY: announcements :158, about_us :174, gallery :182, contact_requests :198, services :271, donation_link :279 in config/capabilities.php, all kind=>module; SIDE_EFFECTS at AppFeaturesCutoverPlan.php:138-148 including 'PUBLIC INTAKE CLOSES' for contact_requests (:147), which I verified is real — Mobile/ContactUsController.php:66 and Api/V1/ContactUsController.php:178 both refuse on moduleIsOff('contact_requests').

BUT THE CLAIM 'DECISIONS.md does not contain it' IS REFUTED. Commit bb675ea adds a 2026-09-17 entry whose Alternatives section records exactly this decision: 'Keep the app drawer on the pivot and leave the switches admin-only. Two switches for one concept, in two places, is what produced an organisation whose admin screen is on and whose app row is off with nobody able to say which was meant. The cutover plan exists because that has already happened.' Item 8 also records that the plan prints 'what switching that module off also means'. The collapse of the two levers into one IS the recorded, reasoned decision; what is genuinely absent is one sentence naming the operational consequence ('after S2b you cannot remove an app row without removing the admin module'). title: The tenancy canary stops watching /features and activated_features at exactly the moment they become tenant-derived
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/config/canary.php:340 ('api/mobile/masjids/{masjid_id}/features' in global_endpoints, justified at :337-341) and :425 ('api/v1/settings' => ['activated_features'] in global_buckets, justified at :415-424); plan §7.6 says only 'Update the canary comments'; HEAD 4a2a57b
scenario: Both exemptions rest on one claim, written at :337-341: 'the pivot's rows are not what this endpoint returns … Two organisations seeing catalog ids 1..11 is the catalog working, not a leak.' After the cutover the payload is computed per organisation from capability_overrides, so that claim is simply false — and both surfaces stay on the canary's do-not-compare lists. A derivation bug that hands org A's switches to org B (a masjidKey collision, a flushFamily that walks the wrong branch, a cached body reused across orgs) would produce precisely the cross-tenant identity checkTenantsGetDistinctAnswers() exists to catch, and the run would still report clean. The plan's remedy is to edit the comment, which leaves the blindness in place.
why_it_matters: The canary is the only automated cross-tenant watch, and the retirement changes these two payloads from shared-catalogue reads into per-tenant derivations. Silencing them through the cutover is the one window where the watch is worth most.
suggested_fix: In the same commit that flips the marker, delete the 'api/mobile/masjids/{masjid_id}/features' line from global_endpoints and the 'api/v1/settings' => ['activated_features'] bucket from global_buckets, and let the run compare both again. If either genuinely still shares catalogue ids, narrow the exemption to the id/name/key fields rather than the whole endpoint.

verification.corrected_title: The /features canary exemption's stated reason is already false at HEAD (the endpoint literally returns pivot rows), but the exemption itself is load-bearing and the cutover does not change what it hides
verification.notes:
PREMISE REFUTED. The finding's claim is that the exemption becomes wrong 'at exactly the moment' the payload becomes tenant-derived. The payload is ALREADY tenant-derived: every row carries `pivot: {masjid_id, feature_id, is_available}` (verified in features-org-1.json), so the comment's sentence 'the pivot's rows are not what this endpoint returns' (config/canary.php:337-343, the entry itself at :343, not :340) is false TODAY, before any cutover. The cutover adds no new blindness — a cross-tenant leak of one org's flags to another was equally invisible before it.

THE SUGGESTED FIX WOULD BREAK THE CANARY. canary.tenants defaults to the two lowest ids, and I diffed the captures: orgs 1 and 2 serve byte-identical /features payloads modulo pivot.masjid_id (all 11 rows, all is_available 1, identical names/keys/timestamps/icons). Deleting the global_endpoints line would make checkTenantsGetDistinctAnswers (TenancyCanary.php:1805-1880) raise same_rows_served_to_two_tenants on every hourly run forever — exactly the false-positive shape the config's own header warns about ('every org missing a donation link will page hourly — which is the bug this setting exists to fix, reintroduced from the other end'). The 'api/v1/settings' => ['activated_features'] bucket at :424 (not :425) is the right model, and the second half of the suggestion (narrow rather than delete) is the only usable part — with the caveat that /features' body is a bare top-level array, so it may not be expressible as a bucket path at all. Downgraded to nit: fix the comment's false sentence, keep the exemption.

title: `navigation_aliases` in config/app_menu.php is never applied — the server stores and emits whichever of the four spellings was typed
location: /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/config/app_menu.php:100-135 (the `navigation_aliases` map, documented as four accepted spellings mapping to two shells); /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Http/Requests/Admin/AppConfig/UpdateAppConfigRequest.php:33 (`in:menu,legacy,side_menu,tabs_drawer`); /Users/moneebsayed/Developer/MasjidWebMS-menu/app/Http/Controllers/Mobile/AppConfigController.php (emits `$row->navigation` raw). HEAD 4a2a57b.
scenario: The config file itself says `AppMenu::registry()` reads only five keys and ignores everything else, so the alias map is documentation. That is fine for the clients — both map unknown values to the new shell, which is the whole argument for accepting four spellings. But nothing canonicalises on the way in. During the R1 rollout an operator rolling one org back sets `legacy` on ios and `tabs_drawer` on android for the same organisation, and `SELECT masjid_id, platform, navigation FROM app_version_settings WHERE navigation IS NOT NULL` no longer answers "which orgs are on the old shell" with one predicate. A later reader of config/app_menu.php could also reasonably believe the server normalises and write a comparison against `'legacy'` that misses half the rows.
why_it_matters: Small, and deliberately chosen — the alternative (an enum column) was considered and rejected for good reasons. It only bites during the rollout, when "which organisations are on legacy right now" is a question somebody asks under time pressure.
suggested_fix: Canonicalise on write in `AdminDashboard/AppConfigController::update` — `$data['navigation'] = config("app_menu.navigation_aliases.{$value}")` with the code-copy fallback, so the column holds only `menu` or `legacy` while the request rule keeps accepting all four. The emitted value is then the canonical one, which both clients already understand, and the aliases stay what they are: an input courtesy, not a stored vocabulary.

verification.notes:
Confirmed, and correctly rated.

Verified: config/app_menu.php:128-134 defines `navigation_aliases` with the four→two map; `grep -rn navigation_aliases` across php/ts/vue returns only the config file and the comment referencing it at UpdateAppConfigRequest.php:32. The rule at UpdateAppConfigRequest.php:33 is `sometimes|nullable|in:menu,legacy,side_menu,tabs_drawer`; AdminDashboard/AppConfigController.php:42 passes `navigation` straight into the update; Mobile/AppConfigController.php:63-64 emits `$row->navigation` raw. So nothing canonicalises, as claimed.

Client-safety is not at risk, which is why nit is right: config/app_menu.php:95-125 documents side_menu and tabs_drawer as "the vocabulary the clients were compiled with" and states "Both clients parse tolerantly: anything they do not recognise is the new shell". Emitting an alias raw is therefore honoured by the client that coined it. The only cost is the one the finding names — `SELECT … WHERE navigation IS NOT NULL` no longer answers "which orgs are on the old shell" with one predicate, during the rollout, under time pressure.

One question for the author that this review cannot settle from this repository (no client source here, so I am not filing it as a finding): the docblock asserts the clients honour their OWN aliases and map unknowns to the NEW shell, but it never asserts they recognise the server's canonical `legacy`. If a client knows only `tabs_drawer`, then setting the canonical `legacy` — the value an admin would naturally pick — maps to unknown, i.e. the NEW shell, and the rollback silently does nothing. Worth one line of confirmation from the iOS/Android source before R1; if it turns out to be true, canonicalising on write the way this finding suggests makes it WORSE, not better, and the right fix inverts (store canonical, emit the client alias).

title: `key` is read by neither shipped mobile client — the review's heaviest artillery is aimed at the wrong field
location: Verified at source: New Masjid System @ acf56cd `Masjid/Models/ObjectModels/Feature.swift` declares `id, name, createdAt, updatedAt, pivot, icon` and no `key` (unchanged at a7217de); burlington-masjid-Android @ master (5f1aa80) `FeaturesResponse.kt` `data class Feature` declares `id, name, created_at, updated_at, pivot, icon` and no `key`.
scenario: BI-8 and R4 treat the U+2019 in `key` as a phone-facing contract byte. Neither shipped client decodes the field. Where it actually matters is `/v1/settings` `activated_features`, which emits `key` verbatim to the web side, and the golden diff. Meanwhile `name` IS load-bearing on both and is the sharper risk: Android declares `val name: String` non-null and vc13 both renders it as the tile label and routes on a lower-cased substring match, and iOS declares `name: String?` optional but the drawer falls back on it. The practical consequence of the misaim is prioritisation — an implementer reading BI-8 protects the key's apostrophe and may reconstruct `name` from the registry, which is the change that actually breaks a phone.
why_it_matters: Small, but the review is long and the author will triage by rating. Getting `name` and `key` the right way round decides which of the two gets the assertion. It also narrows R4 (the seeder's ASCII `quran` key versus production's `qur’an`) from a client risk to what it really is: a provisioning bug that has already mis-seeded org 13, plus a golden-test poisoning risk.
suggested_fix: Restate BI-8 and R4 as: `name` is the phone-facing byte on both clients and must come from the catalogue or the capture, never from `config/app_menu.php`; `key` is a web (`/v1/settings`) and golden-diff byte. Keep both assertions in the contract test, but put the DEFAULT_REGISTRY comment's emphasis on names.

title: S3a's one allowed contract change is now verified safe on both shipped clients — record it before someone re-litigates or, worse, assumes it
location: Verified at source: `Masjid/Models/ObjectModels/Gallery.swift` @ acf56cd — `let id: Int` non-optional, every other field optional (`modelType, modelId, uuid, collectionName, name, fileName, mimeType, disk, conversionsDisk, size, orderColumn, createdAt, updatedAt, originalUrl, previewUrl`), and `manipulations/customProperties/generatedConversions/responsiveImages` already commented OUT; burlington-masjid-Android @ 5f1aa80 `FeatureIcon` — `val id: Int` non-null, `name/file_name/mime_type/original_url/preview_url` all nullable.
scenario: N5-11 and R-M3 both flag S3a's icon shrink (the ~20-key Spatie media row collapsing to `MobileMedia::envelope`'s three-key fallback `{id, original_url, preview_url}`) as an unverified client risk, resting on a comment in MobileMedia.php:81-82 that says "`id` is the only field an older non-optional model requires" — which R-M3 correctly calls a guess. I checked both decoders and the guess is right: on iOS every icon field except `id: Int` is optional and the four heaviest ones are commented out of the struct entirely, and on Android every field except `id: Int` is nullable. The three-key object decodes on both. The residual unknown is the Flutter client, which the retirement lens cites for the 2026-08-28 incident (it force-unwrapped `icon.originalUrl`) — `original_url` survives the shrink, so that specific unwrap is safe, but nothing here checks its icon struct for a non-optional field.
why_it_matters: Recording a verified fact is worth as much as recording a risk, and this one has a deadline: S3a is ~30 days after S2b and the check gets harder once the media rows are deleted. It also converts the plan's "one allowed contract change" from an assertion into a checked claim on two of three clients, which is the right shape for the one place byte-identity is deliberately suspended.
suggested_fix: Record the two decoder facts in the plan beside §7.6's "the icon envelope switches from media URLs to fallback URLs", and replace MobileMedia.php:81-82's guess with the citation. Still do N5-11's ask — assert the icon's key SET against the capture with volatile values normalised, rather than masking the object — because the next field to leave the envelope will not have been checked. Check the Flutter icon model before S3a; it is the one client whose decoder nobody has read.
ft: S3a's one allowed contract change is now verified safe on both shipped clients — record it before someone re-litigates or, worse, assumes it
